entries.english:
2151. The affix लट् comes after a verb when denoting a present action.

Of the affix लट् the letters अ and ट् are indicatory, leaving only ल. This is replaced by other affixes as shown below :--

NOTE:—The word वर्तमान means that which is begun and which has not yet come to an end. The action denoted by a verb in the present tense is yet continuing and has not stopped. As पचति 'he is cooking'; पठति 'he is reading'. So also whatever is constant, regular, uniform, is represented by the Present Indefinite. As तिष्ठन्ति पर्वताः 'the mountains stand'; स्रवन्ति नद्यः 'the rivers flow.'

entries.english:
2152. The tense-affixes called 'la' are used in denoting the object and the agent in the case of Transitive verbs; and after intransitive verbs, they denote the action as well as the agent.

NOTE:—The term ल means the ten affixes known as लट्, लिट्, &c.; ल् is the common element of them all; and these affixes, when stripped of all indicatory letters, leave behind only the letter ल which is thus the common name for them all. The लः in the sûtra, is the nominative plural of ल. By the word च in the sûtra, we draw in the word कर्तरि for 'agent' from the sûtra III. 4. 68 into this. The force of these tense-affixes, when placed after transitive verbs is to denote the object and the agent; and when placed after intransitive verbs, is to denote either 'action' (भाव) or it may denote the 'agent.'

The verb itself denotes the action; to be or to do, generally; or to be or to do, in a particular manner. In the active voice, the affix marks the agent; in the passive voice of a transitive verb, it marks the object; but in the passive form of an intransitive verb, the action itself. Thus ग्रामो गम्यते देवदत्तेन 'the village is gone to by Devadatta'; here गम्यते denotes the object and is in passive construction. ग्रामं गच्छति देवदत्तः 'Devadatta goes to the village'; here the affix ति of गच्छति denotes the agent, and the sentence is in active construction. The verb गम् being a transitive verb, can take both the active and passive constructions or, to use the Sanskrit technical phraseology, the tense-affixes, after transitive verbs, denote the agent and the object. They do not generally denote भाव or action after transitive verbs, that is, transitive verbs are not used impersonally. Let us now give examples of Intransitive verbs; आस्यते देवदत्तेन 'it is seated by Devadatta'; the verb आस्यते denotes merely भाव or 'action'. In other words, we may call this an impersonal construction. देवदत्त आस्ते 'Devadatta sits'; here the verb आस्ते denotes the agent or is in the active voice.

Professor Bohtlingk translates the sûtra thus:—"A finite verb expresses the agent as well as the object; but the Intransitive verbs denote, in addition to that, the Impersonal idea of the action." The word भाव means action considered in the abstract.

Professor Bohtlingk translates this sûtra thus :—In the following sûtras the word ‹?› should be supplied to complete the sense, i. e., the phrase 'in the place of all those endings which are known as the Personal endings of various tenses and moods, and are known in their totality as ‹?›.'

entries.english:
2154. The following are the eighteen substitutes of 'la' :—'tip', 'tas', 'jhi'; 'sip', 'thas', 'tha'; 'mip', 'vas', 'mas'; 'ta', 'âtâm', 'jha'; 'thâs', 'âthâm', 'dhvam'; 'iṭ', 'vahi', 'mahiṅ.'
NOTE:—These are the well-known Conjugational-affixes, called also Personal endings, and are ordained generally after all the ten tenses.

2155. The substitutes of ‹ल› are called parasmaipada.
NOTE:—The word ‹लः› is in the genitive case, and means 'of ‹ल›.' The word 'substitutes' must be supplied to complete the sense.

2156. The nine affixes comprised under the Pratyâhâra taṅ and the two ending in âna (Śânach and Kânach), which are substitutes of ‹ल› are called Âtmanepada.
NOTE:—This debars the previous designation of Parasmaipada. The result is that the first nine substitutes are Parasmaipada and the last nine Âtmanepada.
Then arises the question, what roots should be conjugated in the Parasmaipada and what in the Âtmanepada. The following sûtras, answer that question.
2157. After a root which has an indicatory anudâtta vowel (anudâttet) or an indicatory ṅ (ṅit) in the Dhâtupâṭha, the affixes are those of the Âtmanepada.
entries.note: Devanagari sutra line printed at the foot of page 6; English heading and translation appear on page 7.

entries.english:
2158. After the verb marked with a svarita, (svaritet) or which has an indicatory ñ (ñit) in the Dhâtupâṭha, the terminations of the Âtmanepada are employed, when the fruit of the action accrues to the agent.
NOTE:—The word क्रियाफल is a compound, meaning 'fruit of the action.' When the principal object, for the sake of which, the action is begun, is meant for the agent indicated by the verb, there the âtmanepada is used after verbs having an indicatory ñ or a svarita accent. As यजते 'he sacrifices for himself', पचते 'he cooks for himself.' Here the verb यज् and पच् are marked with svarita accent in the Dhâtupâṭha, and therefore they take the âtmanepada terminations.
Similarly सुते 'he presses the soma-juice,' कुरुते 'he does.' Here the verbs षु and कृ have an indicatory ञ.
In all the above cases, the principal object of the action such as getting heaven by performance of sacrifice, eating of food, &c., is meant for the agent. That is to say, he sacrifices in order that he himself may attain heaven, he cooks in order that he himself may eat, &c.
entries.note: Restored clear embedded Devanagari verb forms from accompanying translations.

entries.english:
2159. After the rest, i. e., after all those verbs not falling under any one of the previous provisions, the terminations of the Parasmaipada are employed, in marking the agent (i. e., in the active voice).
NOTE:—The rules of Âtmanepada have been declared in the 66 sûtras, 12 to 77 of the third Chapter of the First Book of Aṣhṭâdhyâyî. The terminations of the Parasmaipada, which are the general verbal terminations, will come everywhere else, that is to say, where its operation is not debarred by any one of the above-mentioned aphorisms. The present sûtra declares this universal rule. The word śesha or the rest, means that which is the residue of the application of all the previous restrictive rules.

2160. The three triads, in both the sets, Parasmaipada and Âtmanepada, of conjugational affixes (comprised under the general name tiṅ) are called, in order, Lowest (3rd person), the Middle (2nd person), and the Highest (1st person).
NOTE:—Of the 18 conjugational affixes, above given; 9 are Parasmaipadî and 9 are Âtmanepadî. Each of these two classes is subdivided into three sets, according to person.

2161. These three triads, of conjugational affixes, which have received the name of Lowest, &c., are called (as regard the three expressions in each triad) severally "the expression for one" (singular), "the expression for two" (dual), and "the expression for many" (plural).
NOTE:—Of the six triads thus formed, each is divided according to number into three classes, viz., singular, dual, and plural.

2162. When the pronoun yushmad, "thou" understood, and also when the same expressed, is the attendant word in agreement with the verb, then there is the verbal termination called the Middle (2nd person).
NOTE:—This defines the 2nd person of conjugational affixes. As त्वं पचसि thou cookest or पचसि; युवां पचथः or पचथः you two are cooking; यूयं पचथ or पचथ you cook.
entries.note: Restored garbled Devanagari forms in the Note from clear context and translations.

entries.english: 2163. When joke is implied with reference to an action, the verb denoting it is used in the 2nd person; provided that the word manya 'to think,' is the attendant word (upapada) of such verb, and of the
verb manya itself, the affix must be of the 1st person and singular number.

2164. When the pronoun asmad "I," understood, and also when expressed, is the attendant word in agreement with the verb, then there is the verbal termination called Highest or the 1st person.

NOTE: This is clear. As ‹?› "I cook," or merely ‹?›; ‹?› or merely ‹?›.
entries.note: Devanagari examples in Note largely dropped in scan.

entries.english:
2165. In the other cases, namely, where, "thou" or "I" are not the attendant words in agreement with the verb, there is the verbal termination called the lowest (or 3rd person).

NOTE: As ‹?› he cooks, ‹?› they two cook, ‹?› they cook. Now we take up the conjugation of the verb "to be" when the agent is meant, i. e., in the Active Voice. Thus भू + तिप्.

Now apply the following rules :—
entries.note: Devanagari examples in Note partially dropped in scan.

entries.english:
2166. All personal endings (III. 4. 78, S. 2154) and all affixes with an indicatory श् are called 'sârvadhâtuka.'

NOTE: Of course, this applies to the affixes which have been already treated before, namely, the affixes which relate to verbal roots and not to Taddhita affixes, &c. Thus, ‹?›; ‹?› and ‹?› are exceptions. [‹?›].
entries.note: Devanagari citations in Note illegible in scan.

entries.english:
2167. The affix शप् comes after a root, when a sârvadhâtuka follows signifying the agent.

NOTE: In active voice, शप् is employed in the conjugational tenses. This affix, which is technically called a विकरण comes after roots of the भ्वादि class and compound roots formed by सन् &c. (III. 1. 32). The indicatory श् makes it a sârvadhâtuka affix by III. 4. 113, S. 2166, the प् indicates that the vowel has anudâtta accent (III. 1. 4, S. 3709). As भू + शप् + तिप्. The श् and प् are indicatory, the real affix is अ.
entries.note: Repaired serial number misread as 2160; reconstructed grammatical terms spanning page break.

entries.english:
2168. The Guṇa is substituted for the final इक् (इ, उ, ऋ, लृ) vowel of a stem before the affixes called sârvadhâtuka and ârdhadhâtuka (III. 4. 113, S. 2166, &c.) [Those that are not sârvadhâtuka are ârdhadhâtuka].

NOTE: Thus भू + तिप् = भू + शप् + तिप् = भो + अ + ति = भव् + अ + ति = भवति ॥ Similarly भू + तस् = भवतः ॥ The word इक् is read in the sûtra, from I. 1. 3, S. 34.
In forming the 3rd Pers. Pl. भू + झि, the following rule applies :—

2169. अन्त् is substituted for the झ् of an affix.

NOTE:—Therefore भू + झि = भू + शप् + अन्ति = भो + अ + अन्ति = भवन्ति ॥ Similarly भवसि, भवथः, भवथ ॥
In forming the 1st Pers. Sing. भू + शप् + मिप् = भो + अ + मि = भव् + अ + मि ॥
Here the following rule applies :—

2170. The long is substituted for the final अ of a Tense-stem, before a Sârvadhâtuka affix beginning with व् or म् (lit. a consonant of यञ् pratyâhâra).

NOTE:—Thus भव + मि = भवामि ॥ Similarly भवावः, and भवामः ॥
Thus the whole conjugation is :—

लट् Present Tense.

Singular. Dual. Plural.
1st Person भवामि I become भवावः We two become भवामः We become
2nd Person भवसि Thou becomest भवथः You two become भवथ You become
3rd Person भवति He becomes भवतः They two become भवन्ति They become.

We have already mentioned in sûtra I. 4. 106, S. 2163, that in joke, the 1st Person, may be used with the force of 2nd Person. Thus एहि मन्ये ओदनं भोक्ष्यसे, भुक्तः सोऽतिथिभिः "Come here, thou thinkest 'I shall take food'; but it is eaten already by the guest." Here "I think" means "thou thinkest" and "thou shalt eat" is equal to "भोक्ष्ये" "I shall eat."
Similarly in the other examples given above.
In the above sutra I. 4. 106, S. 2163, the phrase मन्यकर्मणि &c., is understood from the previous sûtra. Therefore, when the verb is not in the 2nd person, this construction is not allowed, even though joke be meant. As एहि भो मन्यते भवान् ओदनं भोक्ष्ये &c.! Come respected Sir! (jocularly), your honor thinks "I shall eat rice," &c.
Why do we say "in joke"? The proper person should be used, when simple assertion is intended. Thus एहि मन्यसे ओदनं भोक्ष्य इति भुक्तः सोऽतिथिभिः "Come, thou thinkest 'I shall eat rice'—but it has been eaten by the guest."
NOTE:—This corresponds with the Direct and Indirect narration of the English Grammar. Sanskrit does not admit of Indirect narration, except in the above examples.

Now we take up the लिट् । Thus भू + लिट्. The force of लिट् is to denote the Past time, as shown in the following :—
entries.note: Repaired serial number misprinted/misread as 2172.

entries.english:
2171. The affix लिट् comes after a verb, in the sense of the past, before the commencement of the current day, and unperceived by the narrator.

NOTE: The word 'unperceived' qualifies the words 'past' and 'non-current day' understood in this aphorism.
This लिट् is replaced by तिप् &c. Are these affixes Sârvadhâtuka or Ârdhadhâtuka? By the general rule III. 4. 113, S. 2166, they would have been Sârvadhâtuka, but for the following sûtra.
entries.note: Repaired serial number misread as 2101.
Entry cut off after sutra line at bottom of page 11.

entries.english:
2172. The personal endings of the Perfect are also called 'ârdhadhâtuka.'

NOTE:—The substitutes of ‹लिट्› get the designation of Ârdhadhâtuka, and not that of Sârvadhâtuka. Therefore, they do not take the vikaraṇa or the Mode-affix &c. Further on, even the ‹तिप्› &c. are replaced by the following:—
entries.note: Sutra line omitted at top of page; Devanagari 'लिट्' (OCR 'for') and 'तिप्' (OCR 'far') reconstructed from context.

entries.english:
2173. In the room of the Parasmaipada affixes, the following are substituted in the Perfect Tense :—

Sing. Dual. Plural.
3rd Pers. ṇal (‹णल्›) atus (‹अतुस्›) us (‹उस्›)
2nd Pers. thal (‹थल्›) athus (‹अथुस्›) a (‹अ›)
1st Pers. ṇal (‹णल्›) va (‹व›) ma (‹म›)

NOTE:—The indicatory ‹ल्› in ‹णल्› is for the sake of accent (VI. 1. 193, S. 3676). The indicatory ‹ण्› in ‹णल्› is for the sake of causing ‹वृद्धि› (VII. 2. 25, S. 3065). Thus पपाच, पेचतुः, पेचुः, पेचिथ or पपक्थ, पेचथुः, पेच, पपाच or पपच; पेचिव, पेचिम ।

For the nine substitutes for ‹तिप्› &c. of ‹लिट्› there are ‹णल्› &c. instead. Thus ‹भू + ल् = भू + णल्›.

Then applies the following rule :—
entries.note: Table and Note unbraided from interleaved OCR columns; embedded Devanagari restored.

entries.english:
2174. ‹भू› gets the augment ‹वुक्› (व्) before the tense-affixes of the Aorist and the Perfect, when beginning with a vowel.

NOTE:—This being a nitya rule, supersedes or debars the Guṇa ordained by ‹सार्वधातुकार्धधातुकयोः› (VII. 3. 84, S. 2168) and Vṛiddhi ordained by ‹अचो ञ्णिति› (VII. 2. 115, S. 254). That is to say, the indicatory ‹ण्› of ‹णल्› does not cause Vṛiddhi before ‹वुक्› takes place.

Thus ‹भू + व् + अ = भूव् + अ›.

Now apply the following rules :—
entries.note: Restored missing Devanagari and fixed OCR errors in English.

entries.english:
2175. In the room of the first portion, containing a single vowel, there are two.

NOTE:—Up to Sûtra VI. 1. 12 inclusive it is to be understood that for the first syllable two are to be made, i.e., the first syllable is to be reduplicated. This is an adhikâra sûtra: all the three words viz., ‹एकाचः›, ‹द्वे› and ‹प्रथमस्य› are to be read in the subsequent sûtras up to VI. 1. 12, before the rule of Samprasâraṇa begins. Thus Sûtra VI. 1. 8 says "when ‹लिट्› follows, of an unreduplicated verbal root." The sense of this sûtra is incomplete, unless we supply the three words of this sûtra, when it will read thus: "when ‹लिट्› follows there are two in the room of the first portion, containing a single vowel of an unreduplicated verbal root."
entries.note: Restored Devanagari in Note; corrected typography errors ('i. 6.' -> 'i.e.', 'are is be read' -> 'are to be read').

entries.english:
2176. Of that whose first syllable begins with a vowel, there are two in the room of the second portion containing a single vowel.

NOTE:—This debars the reduplication of the first syllable. In a verbal root beginning with a vowel, and consisting of more than one syllable, the second syllable is to be reduplicated and not the first.

2177. When the tense-affixes of the Perfect follow, there is reduplication of the root, which is not already reduplicated.

NOTE:—The reduplication is either of the first syllable or of the second syllable according as the root begins with a consonant or a vowel.

Thus ‹भूव् + अ› = ‹भूव् + भूव् + अ›.

Now applies the following sûtra by which the first is called Abhyâsa.
entries.note: Restored formula from context; fixed typo 'callod' -> 'called'.

entries.english:
2178. The first of the two is called the Abhyâsa or the Reduplicate.

NOTE:—The word ‹द्वे› in the nominative case is understood here, but for the purposes of this sûtra it is taken in the Genitive case i.e., ‹द्वयोः प्रथमः› "the first of the two" ordained above. The word Abhyâsa occurs in sûtras III. 1. 6, VI. 1. 7 &c.

Thus of ‹भूव् + भूव् + अ›, the first is called Abhyâsa, and therefore the next rule applies to it.
entries.note: Restored Devanagari in Note.

entries.english:
2179. Of the consonants of the reduplicate, only the first is retained, the remainders are dropped.

NOTE:—Thus of ‹भूव् भूव् + अ›, the ‹व्› is elided, and we get ‹भू भूव् + अ›. Then applies the following rules :—
entries.note: Fixed OCR typos 'rea tained' -> 'retained', 'Norn:~' -> 'NOTE:—', and restored Devanagari.

entries.english:
2180. A short is substituted for the long vowel of the reduplicate.

NOTE:—But in the case of भू, this rule is superseded by the next rule. Or we may apply this rule and get ‹भु भूव् + अ›, and then apply the next.
entries.note: Restored Devanagari in Note; third digit missing in sutra line digits.

entries.english:
2181. ‹अ› is substituted for the vowel of the reduplicate of भू in the Perfect.

NOTE:—As बभूव, बभूवतुः, बभूवुः, बभूवे । Why do we say 'in the Perfect'? Observe बुभूषति and बोभूयते ।

The word भवतेः is shown in the sûtra in the Active Voice, therefore the rule will not apply to Passive and Reflexive forms; as अनुबुभूवे कम्बलो देवदत्तेन । This opinion of Kâśikâ, however, is not endorsed by later Grammarians.

Thus ‹भु भूव् + अ› = ‹भ भूव् + अ›.

Then applies the following :—
entries.note: Restored dropped subject '‹अ›'; fixed typos 'satra', 'Norr', 'lator'.

entries.english:
2182. The चर् is also the substitute of झल् letters occurring in a reduplicate syllable, as well as जश् ॥

NOTE:—In a reduplicate syllable, a sonant non-aspirate (‹जश्›) as well as a surd non-aspirate (‹चर्›) is the substitute of a Mute letter. By applying the rule of 'nearest in place' (I. 1. 50, S. 39), we find that sonant non-aspirate (‹जश्›) is the substitute of all sonants ‹झश्› and ‹चर्› is the substitute of all surds. In other words all aspirate letters become non-aspirate. The word ‹जश्› has been drawn into the sûtra by the word ‹च› 'also.'
entries.note: Restored technical Devanagari terms from plain context; entry cut off at page bottom.

entries.english:
The letters are replaced by ‹?› will remain unchanged, and so also an original ‹?› because of the rule of nearness of place.
That is to say:—
‹?› is replaced by ‹?› which is ‹?› letters, and ‹?› by ‹?› But an original ‹?› is replaced by ‹?› not ‹?› but by ‹?›
Thus ‹?›
Then the following doubt arises. The augment ‹?› was added by VI. 4. 88, S. 2174; and the rule VI. 4. 77, S. 271 requires ‹?› augment, and by the following rule is asiddha, and so why should we not have ‹?› also.
entries.note: Tail fragment of entry 2182 continuing from previous page.

entries.english:
2183. The change, which a stem will undergo by the application of any of the rules from this sûtra up to VI. 4. 129, is to be considered as not to have taken effect, when we have to apply any other rule of this very section VI. 4. 23 to 129.

NOTE:—From this sûtra (which is the 22nd sûtra of the fourth chapter of the sixth Adhyâya of Pânini) up to the end of the Fourth Chapter are taught the rules called ‹?›. When two rules of this Âbhîya section simultaneously appear for application in one and the same place, both are applied, one being considered as non-existent for the purposes of the other. Therefore, ‹?› being non-existent, there will be ‹?›, the result of which will be, that in ‹?›, the long ‹?› will be shortened. But this is prevented by the following Vârtika:—

Vârt:—The augments वुक् (VI. 4. 88), and युट् (VI. 4. 68) should however be considered as not asiddha, and rule VI. 4. 77 teaching उवङ् and VI. 4. 82 teaching ‹?› substitution should not be applied simultaneously with them.

Thus भू—बभूव, बभूवतुः, बभूवुः with वुक्, and उपदिदीये, उपदिदीयाथे, उपदिदीविरे, with युट् of VI. 4. 68. In the case of भू, when वुक् is added, there is not the addition of उवङ्, and in the case of दीङ्, when युट् is added, there is not ‹?› ॥

The आ in आभात् has the force of limit inclusive, so that, the asiddha rule applies to the sutras governed by भ.

For fuller explanation of this important sutra, see my Ashtadhyayi.

Now we take up, 2nd Per Sing. बभूव + थल् ॥ Here applies the following sûtra.

2184. An ârdhadhâtuka affix (III. 4. 114 &c) beginning with a consonant (except य), gets the augment इट् (in these rules).

Thus बभूव + थ = बभूव + इ + थ = बभूविथ ॥ So also बभूवथुः, बभूव, बभूविव, बभूविम for Perfect.

3rd Person: Sing. बभूव, Dual बभूवतुः, Plural बभूवुः

entries.english:
2197. तातङ् is optionally substituted for the affixes तु and हि of the Imperative, when benediction is meant.

The substitute तातङ् consists of more than one letter and therefore replaces the whole of तु and हि and not only their final उ or इ. This is by sûtra I. 1. 55 S. 45. But here an objector says, "the substitute तातङ् has an indicatory ङ् and therefore by the sûtra I. 1. 53 S. 43; it will replace only the final, though it consists of more than one letter, just as the substitute ‹?› (VI. 3. 25) replaces only the final of युष्मद् and अस्मद्; or just as the substitute replaces the final of roots only. For the sûtra ङिच्च (I. 1. 53) is an apavada or exception in anticipation to अनेकाल् शित् सर्वस्य (I. 1. 55)."

To this we reply "True; but the sûtra ङिच्च (I. 1. 53) has its scope in affixes like अम्, वस् &c. where ङ् has no other force or indicatory power. But in the case of तातङ् the indicatory ङ् finds its scope in preventing guna and vriddhi (I. 1. 5), and in effecting vocalisation (VI. 1. 16) &c. So the sutra I. 1. 53 applies there only where the indicatory ङ् has no other purpose. In the case of तातङ् it seemed to apply with exhausted force, but that little is also set aside by the subsequent sutra अनेकाल् &c. I. 1. 55. For in the case of तातङ्, the general rule I. 1. 55 and the exceptional rule ङिच्च I. 1. 53 are of equal force, and therefore the maxim विप्रतिषेधे परं कार्यम् will apply, and the subsequent sutra I. 1. 55 will supersede ङिच्च I. 1. 53. Therefore तातङ् replaces the whole affix.

Thus भवतात् "May he be prosperous."

Note:—The affix तातङ् being a substitute of हि, is like हि, and, therefore, rules propounded with regard to हि, will apply to तातङ् also. Thus VI. 4. 105 says that after stems ending in short अ, the हि is elided: therefore, after such words तातङ् should also be elided. Therefore we cannot get the form भवतात् say for भिन्तात्. This objection, however, is futile; for, in the sutra अतो हेः (VI. 4. 105), there is the anuvritti of हि from sutra VI. 4. 101 (हुझल्भ्यो हेर्धिः). So that अतो हेः should be construed as meaning "there is the elision of हि when it is of the form हि, and not when it assumes the form तातङ्".

The object of ङ् in तातङ् is, as we have said above, for the sake of preventing Guna and Vriddhi. It should not be said that the object of ङ् in तातङ् is for the sake of ‹?› by the application of sutra ङिच्च (I. 1. 53), just as the substitutes &c. (VII. 1. 93 and 94) apply to the finals. For by so doing, तातङ् would replace only the उ of तु and the इ of हि, which is not desired. And the case of तातङ् is to be distinguished from आङ्, for in आङ् the ङ् has no other object but to prevent sarvâdesa; but in तातङ् we see that ङ् has another object, namely, the prevention of Guna and Vṛiddhi and having thus found scope, the तातङ् substitute will be governed by the general rule अनेकाल्शित् सर्वस्य (I. 1. 55.)

2198. The personal endings of the Imperative are as those of the Imperfect.

This is an अतिदेश sutra; as in the लङ् there are the affixes तां, तम्, त and म, so also in the लोट्—पचताम्, पचतम्, पचत, पचाव, पचाम ।

Q. If लोट् is like लङ्, why have we not the augment अत्, अट्, or the substitution of जुस् for झि (see III. 4. 111) in the case of लोट् also?

A. The सः of sutra III. 4. 83 is understood in this sutra also, so that the analogy between लोट् and लङ् is a limited analogy and does not make all the rules which are applicable to लङ् equally applicable to लोट् also.

entries.english:
2209. When the Parasmaipada affixes of the Potential follow, then 'yāsuṭ' acutely accented, is their augment, and the termination is regarded as having an indicatory 'ṅ'.

This debars सीयुट्; the उद् of यासुट् is indicatory; the real augment is यास्.

All augments being anudātta, the present sūtra, therefore, especially uses the word udātta, to show that this augment is an exception to the general rule. Though लिङ् has an indicatory ङ, and therefore by the rule I. 1. 56, its substitutes would also be regarded as having an indicatory ङ, the repetition of the word ङित् in this sūtra, shows the existence of the paribhāshā “that the ङ belonging to लिङ् does not influence its substitutes;” in other words, the substitutes of ‹?›, are not to be regarded as having an indicatory ङ (‹?›). Or it indicates that the prohibition of अनल्विध of sūtra I. 1. 56 does sometime apply to the letters of an anubandha, in other words, the operations required by a particular anubandha letter do not sometimes take place, when the affix having that anubandha-letter is replaced by another which has it not. This we further infer from the employment of the anubandha ‹?› in the substitute which replaces the लिङ् affix ‹?› (see III. 1. 83). The substitute could have been very well enunciated as ‹?›, for replacing a लिङ् affix, it would have been ‹?› by virtue of ‹?› (I. 1. 56). In the Potential, the ‹?› of ‹?› is elided by VII. 2. 79. So we get the forms ‹?›, and by applying III. 4. 108 and VI. 1. 96, ‹?›. For the Benedictive लिङ् the sūtra III. 4. 116. S. 2216, applies.

Thus ‹?›

entries.english:
2211. In the sârvadhâtuka Liṅ (i. e. Potential), the स which is not final (i. e. the स् of the augments यास् and सीयुट्), is elided.
What is the स which is not final? The स् of the augments, यास् and सीयुट्. Thus both स्'s are elided. The स् of सीयुट् is heard in the Benedictive; and better still in the âtmanepada.
Thus भू+शप्+या+त्

2212. After a Present stem ending in short अ, इय् is substituted for the sârvadhâtuka या (i. e., the augment of the Potential).
Thus भू+शप्+यास् + त् = भव+यास् + त् = भव+इय्+त् ॥ The अ+इ become guṇa and the य् is elided by VI. 1. 66. S. 873. (लोपो व्योर्वलि) | Thus we have भवेत् ॥
NOTE:—The objector may say, the form भवेत् will be so by the elision of अ under VI. 4. 48, (अतो लोपः) and so there is no necessity of reading the anuvṛtti of sârvadhâtuka in this sûtra; for when अ is elided by VI. 4. 48, in the case of ârdhadhâtuka या the present rule cannot apply, as there is no base left which ends in अ. To this we reply, this is not a good reason: for then in the case of चिकीर्षेत् and also, the rule (VII. 3. 101) would apply, and the अ would require to be lengthened. But that is not so. The fact is that the present sûtra debars rule VII. 3. 101. Therefore, as this substitute debars the lengthening of VII. 3. 101, so it would debar the lopa of VI. 4. 48. Therefore, if the anuvṛtti of sârvadhâtuka be not read into this sûtra, the substitute इय् would apply to ârdhadhâtuka also, and the lopa-elision VI. 4. 48, would not help, as that would be superseded by this special rule. Therefore the anuvṛtti of "sârvadhâtuka" should be read into this sûtra.
TEXT:—The above is stated on general grounds. But if the maxim मध्येऽपवादाः पूर्वान् विधीन् बाधन्ते नोत्तरान् (Apavâdas that are surrounded by the rules which teach operations that have to be superseded by the apavâda operations; supersede only those rules that precede, not those that follow them) be applied here, then the present sûtra would supersede only the preceding sûtra VI. 4. 48, and not the following sûtra VII. 3. 101 which would not be superseded by the present sûtra. In this view also, the lopa alone being superseded, and not the dīrgha, there would have been lengthening in भवेत् &c. by the subsequent sûtra, hence the anuvṛtti of 'sârvadhâtuka' must be read into this sûtra. So also 3rd Dual. भवेताम् ॥

This debars अन्त् (VII. 1. 3). The ज् is इत् or indicatory.
Thus भू+शप्+या+झि = भव+यास्+उस् = भव+या+उस् (the स् being elided by VII. 2. 79. S. 2211).
Now the sûtra अतो येयः VII. 2. 80. S. 2212, has been explained by Eastern Grammarians thus "after a stem in अ, the या is replaced by इय्". According to this interpretation, we get भव + इया (the य् being elided by VII. 2. 79) + उस् ॥
Then the following sûtra requires आ+उ=ओ or भवेयुः ॥

2214. For the अ or आ (not standing at the end of a Pada or full word) + उ of उस the Tense affix the second vowel is the single substitute.
NOTE:—The आत् is understood here. This debars the guṇa taught in VI. 1. 87. Thus भिक्षा+उ=भिक्षु, हिंसा+उ=हिंसु, (उ of उस) अदुः All these are examples of उस.
Thus दा+आङ्+झि (the झि of III. 4. 108) (II. 4. 77) + जुस् (III. 4. 110) = अदा+उस् = अदुः ॥ अ+या+झि+या+उस् (VI. 4. 111): The उस is also the substitute of झि in लिट् (Perfect) see III. 4. 82. When the preceding vowel is not अ or आ, this rule does not apply. Thus the 3rd per. pl. of the Perfect of बिभी is:—बिभ्युः So also from भी we have बिभी + उस् = बिभ्युः ॥ The word अपदान्तात् 'not being final in a Pada' does strictly speaking, serve no good purpose in this sûtra. For the affix can never be added to a Pada, it must always be added to a stem, that has not yet risen to the rank of a Pada. If, however, उस be taken as the syllable उस (whether an affix or part of an affix or not), then the limitation of अपदान्तात् becomes valid. Thus प्र+उस्त=प्रोस्त, प्र+उषित=प्रोषित ॥ Most likely this word has been read here for the sake of the subsequent sûtra or because उस syllable is taken here and not merely the affix ॥
For here उस comes after the आ, and therefore there should be the single substitute of the form of the second and अतो येयः will find no scope here, for there is no या and the form would be भवोयुः To this there are two replies. First according to Eastern Grammarians who interpret अतो येयः "After a stem in अ, the या of यासुट् is replaced by इय्". In this view, the स् being elided by VII. 2. 79, we have इया+उस्, and here the sûtra अतो येयः must apply first and then the present sûtra, because VII. 2. 80, is a subsequent sûtra to the present in the order of Pāṇini; and because it is a nitya rule, because it will apply whether the combination required by VI. 1. 96, has taken place or not. Thus we get भव + इया + उ = भवेयुः ॥ For if the pararūpa sandhi takes place first, then भव+या+उ becomes भवोस्, and so there is no occasion for the application of अतो येयः, for there is no या to be replaced, and so there is no इय् and we get भवोयुः ॥
The other view is, that the pararūpa sandhi of the present sûtra is antaraṅga, because the operation ordained by it is inside that of VII. 2. 80: and therefore it ought to apply first. But in the present case, there is no occasion for its operation, because the whole या is replaced by इय् according to our interpretation.
Thus the sûtra अतो येयः is an apavâda to the rule requiring the elision of स् taught by the sûtra VII. 2. 79. Thus we get भव+इय्+स्+उस्, and here there is no preceding अ, and so the present sûtra cannot apply.
The word इयः in the sûtra is formed by इय्+स्; and is exhibited without any case-termination. Others say, the word is इयः the sixth case of इ formed on the analogy of सख्युः by the elision of य् (VI. 4. 140). Then भव+इय्+उस् = भव+इ+उस् (VIII. 3. 19) after this elision, there ordinarily would take place no sandhi as this elision is considered asiddha (VIII. 2. 1) for the purposes of VI. 1. 87. Contrary to this general rule, however, the sandhi takes place here and

entries.english:
2215. When the sense is that of Benediction, the substitutes of 'liṅ' are called 'ârdhadhâtuka', i. e. the personal endings of the Benedictive are 'ârdhadhâtuka'.

This debars these affixes from being called sârvadhâtuka. Being ârdhadhâtuka they take the augment, and before these affixes the root does not take the Vikaraṇas &c. Thus from the root लू 'to cut', we have in the आशीर्लिङ्, लविषीष्ट ; and from the root पू 'to purify', पविषीष्ट. But in the विधिलिङ् (Potential), we have the proper Vikaraṇas &c. as लुनीयात् पुनीयात् ।

2216. The augment 'yâsuṭ' comes after that 'liṅ' also which denotes benediction, and it is acutely accented, and is treated as if it had an indicatory 'k'.

The ‹?› of this sûtra refers to the personal affixes of the Benedictive mood and not to the augment yâsuṭ, for that would have been unnecessary, being already ‹?› by the last rule. ṅit and kit are equal in prohibiting guṇa and vṛiddhi, but kit is distinguished from ṅit inasmuch as ṅit causes the guṇa of ‹?› (VII. 3. 85), and also there is distinction between them with regard to the change of semi-vowel to vowel (VI. 1. 15 and 16). Thus, ‹?›; and ‹?›, ‹?› and ‹?›. In the Potential, ‹?› (no samprasâraṇa); in the Benedictive, ‹?› (vocalisation). So also ‹?› in the Potential.

Thus भू + यास् + त् । Then the त् is elided by VIII. 2. 29. S. 380. Thus we get भू + यास् । What is the force of making the augment kit? The next sûtra answers this.

2217. And that, which otherwise would have caused guṇa or vṛiddhi, does not do so, when it has an indicatory क् or ङ्.

Thus there is no guṇa of the उ of भू. So we have.

NOTE:—The indicatory ङ् of the verbal tense affixes i. e., लङ्, लिङ्, लुट्, लृट्, is an exception to this rule of ‹?›. This is an inference deduced from III. 4. 104 S. 2216 which declares "when the sense is that of benediction, then the augment yâsuṭ of liṅ is as if it were distinguished by an indicatory k." There would have been no necessity of making yâsuṭ kit, if liṅ were a ṅit, but the very fact of making yâsuṭ kit indicates by implication or jñâpaka that the final ङ् of liṅ, &c. does not make these tense affixes ṅit. Thus in लङ् or Imperfect tense we have अचिनोत् "he collected" (चि + लङ् = अ + चि + श्नु + तिप् = अ + चि + नु + ति = अ + चि + नो + त् = अचिनोत्).

2218. The affix 'Luṅ' comes after a verb in the sense of past time.

The 'Luṅ' forms what is known as aorist. It is in fact the name of the aorist, as the whole of this affix is replaced by other personal terminations. See III. 1. 43 and subsequent sûtras.

"The aorist has reference to a past time indefinitely or generally, without reference to any particular time. An action done before today is expressed by the perfect or imperfect; whatever remains for the aorist is, therefore, to express a past action, done very recently, say, in the course of the current day or having reference to a present act... Aorist, therefore, merely implies the completion of an action at a past time generally, and also an action done at a very recent time."

2219. The affix 'Luṅ' comes after a verb when the word 'mâṅ' is used in connection with it.

This sets aside all other tense affixes. As मा कार्षीत् 'let him not do', मा हार्षीत् 'let him not take'.

How have we then the Imperative and the Future tenses in the following sentence instead of the Aorist ? मा भवतु तस्य पापं मा भविष्यति । This sentence is against good usage. Or, we may explain it by saying that there is another मा which has not the indicatory ṅ ; and with that मा, other tenses may be used.

The augment अ is elided after the prohibitive particle मा, by VI. 4. 71.

2220. When the word 'mâṅ' is followed by 'sma', the affix 'Laṅ' as well as 'Luṅ' may be employed after a verbal root.

By च we introduce लुङ् into the aphorism. Thus मास्म करोत् or कार्षीत् 'let him not make'; मास्म हरत् or हार्षीत् 'let him not take'.

2221. When लुङ् follows, the affix च्लि is added to the verbal root.

It debars the Mode-affixes शप् and the rest.

2222. Of च्लि, सिच्, is the substitute.

The इ of सिच् is for the sake of pronunciation, the च् is for accent, and the real affix is स्.
2223. There is luk-elision of the affix सिच् in the Parasmaipada, after the verbs गा 'to go', स्था 'to stand', the verbs called घु (I. 1. 20), पा 'to drink' and भू 'to be.'

2224. भू 'to be' and सू 'to be born' get no guṇa before an immediately following Personal ending which is Sârvadhâtuka.

The सू refers to the Adâdi root सू (21) in which the Present character is dropped, and does not refer to Divâdi षू (24) or Tudâdi षूङ् (115) roots because in these two, the mode-affixes and intervene between the तिङ् and the root, and so the root is not immediately followed by the तिङ् ॥

entries.english:
2225. A single consonantal sârvadhâtuka affix gets the augment ईट् after 'to be' and after the Aorist character सिच् when the ‹?› of अस् and सिच् are not elided.

The सिच् plus अस् have become a Samâhâra Dvandva compound, declined in the Ablative Singular. The ‹?› of सिच् has not become ‹?› and then ‹?› is considered here as a Bha base by Sûtra-license.

The words of this sûtra require a little explanation. It consists of four words 1. अस्ति (an Indeclinable meaning "when present") 2. सिच्, 3. अप्रुक्ते, 4. ‹?›. The सिच् has become ‹?› a Samâhâra Dvandva compound meaning "the Mode-affix सिच् and the root to be". In forming the compound, the word सिच् is not treated as a Pada, but as a Bha; and so the ‹?› is not changed to ‹?› or ‹?› i. e., the compound is not ‹?›, as in वाग्रथौ । This is a Sûtra license.

The word अस्ति is an Indeclinable meaning "when present"; i. e., when अस् and सिच् are present as सिच् and अस् without the elision of ‹?› Then this ‹?› is compounded with सिच् as a Karmadhâraya compound, and we have ‹?› Then this compound takes the Ablative affix and so we have ‹?› But this Ablative ending is elided as a Sûtra-anomaly and we have ‹?› literally meaning "after sich and as, when existing (as such)".

This sutra however does not apply here, because सिच् is non-existent. Therefore we have, अभूत्, अभूताम् &c.

As आसीत्, आसीः ; अवादीत्, अवादीः । Why do we say consonantal? Observe ‹?›. Why do we say a single-consonant affix? Observe ‹?› and अभूताम् ॥

Vârt:— Prohibition of the sthânivad-bhâva must be stated when ‹?› is substituted for ‹?› (III. 4. 84), and ‹?› for अस् (II. 4. 52), before the augment ‹?› Therefore not here ‹?› and ‹?› The word ‹?› is thus formed.

‹?›

NOTE:— This round about explanation of Bhattoji Dikshit is for the following reason:—

According to Ancient Grammarians the word अस्तिसिच् is a Samâhâra Dvandva of asti and sich, meaning "the verb अस् and the affix सिच्". And the Ablative singular of asti-sich is asti-sichas meaning "after the verb as and the affix sich." But the compound asti-sich will require the Samâsânta ‹?› (V. 4. 106) and the word would be asti-sicha, a vowel-ending prâtipadika. If it be said that the Samâsânta is anitya, then there is this difficulty that सिच् should be placed first in forming the compound, i. e., we should have सिजस्ति because सिच् consists of fewer letters than अस्ति (अल्पाच्तरम् II. 2. 34). If it be said that this rule is also anitya, because Pânini himself violates it in the sûtra ‹?› (IV. 4. 118), where samudra is placed first and not abhra; even then when ‹?› is changed to ‹?› in the example ‹?›, this sûtra will apply, because ‹?› is considered as sthânivat to ‹?› And similarly in ‹?› and ‹?› the elided सिच् will be sthânivat and so there will be ‹?› To prevent all these difficulties, Bhattoji has given the above explanation.

entries.english:
2226. (In those tenses which are marked with an indicatory 'ङ्') 'jus' is the substitute of 'jhi', when it comes after an Aorist in 'sich', or the Imperfect of a reduplicated verb, or the root 'vid' (to know).

This would make अभू+झि = अभू+जुस्

But this does not apply, on account of the following sûtra.

2227. When सिच् is elided, then the झि is not changed to जुस् except when the stem ends in long आ ॥

The Present Sûtra says that after verbs in which सिच् has been elided, जुस् does not replace झि in the case of any other verb than that which ends in long आ; it is thus a niyama rule.

Thus, by rule II. 4. 77, S. 2223, सिच् is elided after the verb भू, but as भू does not end in long आ, its 3rd person plural Aorist will not be in जुस् ।

Thus, अभूवन् । Here, by the last rule, and on the maxim that though सिच् is elided, yet its force remains, (I. 1. 62 S. 262) जुस् would have replaced झि; but the present sûtra prohibits that. But where the सिच् is not elided, there, of course, जुस् does come. Thus अकार्षुः, अहार्षुः ।

Thus we have भू+झि = अभू+झि (झोऽन्तः VII. 1. 3 S. 2174.) = अभू+अन् (इतश्च III. 4. 100 S. 2207) = अभू + वुक् (भुवो वुग् VI. 4. 88, S. 2169) + अन् (संयोगान्तस्य लोपः VIII. 2. 23. S. 54) = अभूवन् ॥

The 2nd Per. Sing. is अभू+सिच्+सिप् = अभू+०+स् = अभूः 2nd Per. Dual is अभू+सिच्+थस् = अभू+०+थस् + तस् = अभूतम् । In the same manner अभूत ॥

The First Pers. sing is अभू+सिच् + मिप् = अभू+०+अम् = अभू+वुक्+अम् = अभूवम् So also अभूव, अभूम ॥

Thus मा भवान् भूत् or मा स्म भवत् भूद् वा ॥

entries.english:
Now we take up the conjugation of भू in लृङ्.
"The force of लृङ् is to denote a condition antecedent added to futurity, as shown in the following sutra,
entries.note: Tail fragment of entry 2228 preceding SK 2229.

entries.english:
2229. Where there is a reason for affixing 'Lin,' the affix 'Lrin' is employed in the Future tense, when the non-completion of the action is to be understood.

The words 'in denoting future time' are understood here. The reasons for affixing लिङ् are such, as, cause and effect &c. mentioned in sûtra III. 3. 156 and 157 &c. The लृङ् is called the conditional tense. "It comes in the conditional sentences in which the non-performance of the action is implied; or where the falsity of the antecedent is implied as a matter of fact. It usually corresponds to the English pluperfect conditional, and must, in Sanskrit, be used in both the antecedent and the consequent clauses".

Thus सुवृष्टिश्चेदभविष्यत् तदा सुभिक्षमभविष्यत् "if there had been good rain, then there would have been plenty of food; or if there were to be good rain then there would be plenty of food". It is implied that there was not good rain, nor consequent plenty: or that the occurrence of good rain is dubious, and the desirable consequence equally so.

So also here, दक्षिणेन चेद्यास्यन् न शकटं पर्य्याभविष्यत् 'if he were to go by the right side, the carriage would not be upset'; यदि कमलकरं व्यहास्यन् न शकटं पर्य्याभविष्यत् 'if he were to call Kamalaka (which he will not), the carriage would not be upset'; नाभोज्यत भवान् घृतेन यदि मत्समीपम् आगमिष्यत् 'you would eat food with clarified butter, if you (were to) come to me (but you will not come).'

All these sentences refer to future time. The non-upsetting is a future contingency and is an effect, the cause of which is the calling of Kamalaka. The speaker—having apprehended the cause and effect, and having also learned from other sources that such an effect will not take place, that is to say, that Kamalaka will not be called, and the carriage will be upset—has employed this conditional tense to express his idea. The whole sentence यदि कमलकरं व्यहास्यन् &c. really gives this sense:—That both actions, 'the calling' and 'the non-upsetting', which are subjects of a future time, and which are related as cause and effect, will not be completed; that neither Kamalaka will be called, nor the impending fate averted from the carriage. The sûtra may also be thus rendered according to Professor Böhtlingk:—In conditional sentence, which would require a Potential according to III. 3. 156 the conditional tense is used, if the sense is that of Future time, when the action is not complete.

Thus भू + लृङ् = भू + ल् + तिप् (III. 1. 33. S. 2186.) = अ + भू + स्य + ति = अ + भो + स्य + ति = अ + भव् + इ + ष्य + ति = अभविष्यत् ॥

Singular. Dual. Plural.
Third person. अभविष्यत् अभविष्यताम् अभविष्यन्
Second person. अभविष्यः अभविष्यतम् अभविष्यत
First person. अभविष्यम् अभविष्याव अभविष्याम

Thus we have conjugated भू in all the लकारs except the Vedic लेट् ॥

The author now gives some rules about the adding of Prepositions to the verbs and the changes of meaning and conjugation which such addition induces.

The first question is, where are those prepositions to be placed. In English they are generally placed after the verb; in the Vedas they are placed any where in the sentence; but Panini restricts the use in Classical Sanskrit by the following :—
entries.note: Devanagari serial number misprinted as 2226; corrected to 2229.

entries.english:
2230. The particles called gati and upasarga are to be employed before the verbal root: (that is to say, they are prefixes).

The word ते has been employed to include the term उपसर्ग also.

The list of prepositions has already been given in the sûtra उपसर्गाः क्रियायोगे (I. 4. 59 and 60; S. 22 and 23). Thus प्र + भवानि (Imperative 1st Pers. Sing.).

Here applies the following sûtra.

2231. The न of आनि, the affix of the Imperative, 1st Person, is changed into ण, when it follows a letter competent to cause such a change, standing in an Upasarga.

The word आनि is the 1st person singular termination of the Imperative. Thus प्रभवाणि. Similarly "Let us cultivate or sow."

Note:—Why do we say 'of the Imperative'? Observe प्रवपाणि पात्राणि. Here आनि is the neuter plural termination, and the word means प्रकीर्णानि व्रीह्यादीनि येषु तानि.

According to Padamanjari, the employment of the word लोट् in the sûtra is redundant. For without it also आनि would have meant the Imperative affix, and not the Neuter termination, on the maxim of अर्थवद्ग्रहणे &c. Moreover in the noun प्रवपाणि, प्र is not an upasarga at all, on the maxim यत् क्रियायुक्ताः प्रादयः तं प्रति गत्युपसर्गसंज्ञे भवतः ॥

Vart:— The Upasarga दुर् is not to be treated as an upasarga, when षत्व or णत्व is to be effected. That is to say, the र् of दुर् does not cause the subsequent स् or न् to be changed to ष् and ण्, respectively. Thus दुःस्थितिः, दुर्भवानि ॥

Vart:— The Indeclinable word अन्तर् should be treated as an upasarga for the application of (1) अ विधिः namely the affixing of अ by III. 3. 106. S. 3283. आतश्चोपसर्गे, as अन्तर् + धा + अ = अन्तर्धा, (2) किविधिः namely the application of कि by उपसर्गे घोः किः (III. 3. 92. S. 3270), as अन्तर् + धा + कि = अन्तर्धिः (3) णत्व विधि as अन्तर्भवाणि ॥
entries.note: Devanagari serial number misprinted as ३२३२, corrected to 2231.

entries.english:
2232. In the remaining verbs, optionally the न of नि is replaced by ण, when it is preceded by an upasarga competent to cause the change; provided that, in the original enunciation, the verb has not an initial क or ख, nor ends with ष ॥

The words नेः and उपसर्गात् are understood in the sûtra. The word शेषे means verbs other than those mentioned in VIII. 4. 17 S. 2285 namely, other than गद, नद &c. Thus प्रणिभवति or प्रनिभवति, प्रणिभिनत्ति or प्रनिभिनत्ति ॥

Why do we say अकखादौ "not beginning with क or ख"? Observe प्रनिखनति, प्रनिकषति ॥ Here there is no change.
entries.note: Entry incomplete at end of page 38.

entries.english:
Why do we say अभवान्त: “not ending in ‹?›” ? Observe ‹?› ॥

Why do we say "in original enunciation"? So that the prohibition may apply to forms like प्रणिचकार, प्रणिचखाद, प्रतिषेधयति (VIII. 2. 41 S. 295). Here, &c., do not begin with ‹?› or ‹?› nor does ‹?› end with ‹?› but with ‹?› (VIII. 2. 41) but in the Dhâtupâṭha the verb ‹?› and ‹?› begin with ‹?› and ‹?› and ‹?› ends with ‹?›, and hence the rule will not apply. So also in ‹?› and ‹?› from the root ‹?› Here though the verb now ends with ‹?› by VIII. 2. 36, S. 295, yet in the original enunciation or Dhâtupâṭha, it ends with ‹?›.

An objector may say "what is the necessity of using the word optionally in the sutra, when the present sûtra is governed by the word संहितायाम् (VI. 3. 114 S. 1035). So where there is no samhitâ, there will be no ‹?› change ; And as upasargas are not compounded with the verb before which they are placed, there is no compulsory samhitâ." To this we reply "No. The samhitâ is compulsory, even though the upasarga may not be compounded with the root as here." The following verse mentions this :—

Verse.
The Samhitâ is compulsory (1) in a Pada (complete word), (2) in a dhâtu (verb) preceded by an upasarga; and (3) in compounds (Samâsa). But the Samhitâ is optional between the words of a sentence.

The root ‹?› means “to be” in the Dhâtupâṭha, and "to increase" &c. All these meanings are merely illustrative. For we find in the example ‹?› "By sacrifice Heaven is produced or attained," that the root has the meaning of 'to produce.' So every root has many meanings. The upasargas when added to a root, do not give it a new meaning, but limit the particular meaning. In other words, out of many meanings that a root possesses, a particular meaning is specified by the employment of a particular upasarga.

Thus ‹?› "He conquers," अनुभवति "He experiences", अभिभवति "He defeats", ‹?› "It is possible", ‹?› "He is overpowered", उद्भवति "It springs forth", परिभवति "He subdues."

Therefore we have the following verse: By an upasarga the sense of the root is forcibly modified, such as the root ‹?› "to lose", in प्रहार means “a blow”, आहार “food”, संहार “destruction”, विहार “sport”, परिहार “avoidance”.

Here ends the conjugation of the Parasmaipada root भू ॥
entries.note: Continuation from preceding page; tail of entry 2232.

entries.english:
ATMANEPADA.

Now we take up the conjugation of the root एधृ "to increase." The thirty-six roots beginning with एध and ending with ‹?› are Anudatteta. That is, the final ‹?› in एध &c. has anudatta accent and is indicatory or इत्.

First we conjugate it in लट् Present Tense, 3rd Pers. sing.

Thus एध् + त = एध् + शप् + त = एध् + अ + त

Here applies the following sutra :—

2233. The substitute ए replaces the last vowel, with the consonant that follows it, of the 'Atmanepada' substitutes of that ‘la’ which has an indicatory 'ट्'.

Thus एध् + त = एध् + त् + ए = एधते ॥ The 3rd Pers. Dual is एध् + आताम्

Now apply the following sutras :—
entries.note: Introductory text to Atmanepada section precedes sutra heading; third number in Ashtadhyayi reference is illegible in scan.

entries.english:
2234. A Sârvadhâtuka (III. 4. 113 S. 2166) affix not having an indicatory प् is like ङित् ॥

The affix आताम् is therefore ङित्, and consequently the following sûtra applies.

2235. For the आ being a portion of a Sarvadhatuka Personal ending which is ङित् (i.e. आते, आथे, आताम् and आथाम्), coming after a verbal stem ending in short अ, there is substituted इय् ॥

Thus एध् + आताम् = एध् + अ + इय् + ताम् = एध् + इताम् (लोपो व्योर्वलि VI. 1. 66 S. 873) = एधेताम् = एधेते ॥ So also एधन्ते ॥ The 2nd Pers. Sing. is एध् + थास्. Now applies the following sûtra :—
entries.note: Embedded Devanagari derivation reconstructed from clear context.

entries.english:
2236. The word 'se' is the substitute of 'thas' in those tenses that have an indicatory 'ट्'.

Thus एध् + शप् + थास् = एध् + अ + से = एधसे ॥ Similarly एधेथे, एधध्वे ॥ The 1st Pers. Sing. is एध् + इट् = एध् + अ + ए (III. 4. 79 S. 2233) = एधे (VI. 1. 97 S. 191). So also एधावहे, एधामहे ॥

Conjugation of एध् 'to increase' in लट् Present Tense.
3rd Person. Singular एधते Dual एधेते Plural एधन्ते
2nd Person. Singular एधसे Dual एधेथे Plural एधध्वे
1st Person. Singular एधे Dual एधावहे Plural एधामहे
entries.note: Devanagari forms in Lat conjugation table restored from immediately preceding derivation.

entries.english:
लिट् Perfect Tense.

In लिट् we have एध् + त. Here applies the following :—

2237. The affix आम् is used when लिट् follows, after a root beginning with a vowel (except अ or आ) and which has a heavy vowel, but not after the root ऋच्छ् 'to go'.

The म् of आम् is not इत् or indicatory. This we infer from आम् being taught with regard to the roots कास् and आस् in sutra कास्प्रत्ययादाममन्त्रे लिटि (III. 1. 35 S. 2308) and दयायासश्च (III. 1. 37 S. 2324). If म् were indicatory, then कास् + आम् = का + म् + आ + स् = कास् ; similarly आस् + आम् would have remained आस्; for the force of indicatory म् is to place the affix after the penultimate vowel. So there would have been no need of teaching आम् after कास् and आस् roots, as it can produce no change in them. The fact, that it is so taught, leads to the conclusion (jñâpaka) that म् is not indicatory.

Thus एध् + त = एधाम् + त ॥ Now applies the following sutra.
entries.note: Introductory text to Lit tense precedes sutra heading; embedded Devanagari in jnapaka argument reconstructed from clear context.

entries.english:
2238. There is luk-elision in the room of that tense affix (लिट्) which comes after आम् of the Perfect.

Thus एधाम् + त = एधाम् + 0

Then the following sutra appears.

entries.note: Sutra serial number misprinted as 2238 in source, corrected to 2239; entry cut off at bottom of page batch.

entries.english:
2239. After a verb which ends with आम्, the verb 'to do' is annexed, when लिट् follows.

After the verbs formed by taking the आम् augment, the perfect tense of कृञ् is added, to form their Perfect. The word कृञ् includes also the verbs भू and अस्. This we infer from the next sûtra आम्प्रत्ययवत्कृञोऽनुप्रयोगस्य (I. 3. 63 § 2240) from the fact that root कृञ् is specifically mentioned in it as an anuprayoga or auxiliary verb. For the sûtra I. 3. 63 is confined to कृञ् anuprayoga, implying thereby that there are other anuprayoga verbs also which are not governed by that sûtra I. 3. 63. In fact, the word कृञ् of the present sûtra is a Pratyâhâra or a formula, formed with the कृ of the sûtra भूततद्भावे कृभ्वस्तियोगे संपद्यकर्तरि च्विः (V. 4. 50) and the ञ् of the sûtra कृञः सातिदाचिष्वलोपः (V. 4. 58), and thus, as a pratyâhâra कृञ् means and includes कृ, भू and अस् also. The roots कृ, भू and अस् denote action in general, while the bases in आम् such as कास् denote a particular action; and hence when the auxiliary कृ, भू or अस् is combined with आम् ending base, the two senses, namely the general sense of the auxiliary and the particular sense of the आम् ending verb, coalesce into one and give one full indivisible sense. Thus the syntactical connection is indissoluble or abheda-anvaya.

Therefore, though the root संपद् is included in the Pratyâhâra कृञ् (for that pratyâhâra extends over eight sûtras V. 4. 50 to V. 4. 58 and संपद् is in sûtra V. 4. 53) yet that root is not applicable here, because it does not denote mere action and so can never form an abheda-anvaya with the main verb.

Now the auxiliary कृञ् because it has an indicatory ञ् would take the affixes of the Parasmaipada when the fruit of the action accrues to another, by force of I. 3. 72; but it is prevented by the following.
entries.note: Sutra line of 2239 was printed on preceding page 41; page 42 opens with remainder of Sanskrit vritti, followed by the English heading 2239.

entries.english:
2240. When the principal verb that takes the affix आम् is Âtmanepadî, then the verb कृञ् when subjoined thereto as an auxiliary, will similarly be Âtmanepadî, even when the fruit of the action does not accrue to the agent.

This sûtra applies where the fruit of the action does not accrue to the agent. The question is what conjugation, parasmai or âtmanepada, do the auxiliaries take, in forming the periphrastic perfect? This sûtra supplies the answer. The auxiliary कृ follows the conjugation of its principal, the other auxiliaries do not. Thus the root एध् (to increase, prosper) is âtmanepadî, therefore in forming the periphrastic perfect, the verb कृ will be also in the âtmanepada. But the other auxiliaries भू and अस् retain their own peculiar conjugation and are not influenced by the conjugation of their principal. Thus एधांबभूव, एधामास.

The word âm-pratyaya of the sûtra is a Bahuvrîhi, in which the force is that of atadguṇa-saṃvijñâna. That is, the root without the affix आम् is meant here, and not along with or qualified by the actual presence of आम्: it means 'that after which the affix आम् comes.' Of the verb kriñ, when subjoined to another as an auxiliary, the termination is that of the âtmanepada, like the verb that takes the affix आम् ॥

Note:—If this sûtra enjoined a rule of injunction (vidhi), then there would be the termination of the âtmanepada even in examples like ‹?› and ‹?› where the fruit of the action accrues to the agent. This is no valid objection to the present sûtra. It is to be interpreted in both ways, that is, both as a vidhi (a general injunction) and a niyama (a restrictive injunction). How is that to be done? Because the word "pûrvavat" of the immediately preceding Ashțâdhyâyî sûtra is to be read in the present aphorism also and thus there are two sentences. That is, there is âtmanepada of the auxiliary, when the Primary verb is âtmanepadî, but not the contrary. Thus चकास् (to appear with great splendour) is originally parasmaipadî and the auxiliary after it will be parasmaipada even when the fruit of the action accrues to the agent, as चकासाञ्चकार (he appeared with great splendour). The second explanation, in that case, will be for the sake of establishing a niyama or restrictive rule.

It has already been said above, that the auxiliary verbs कृ, भू and अस् are used in forming the periphrastic perfect. This is done by force of the aphorism III. 1. 40 § 2239 कृञ्चानुप्रयुज्यते लिटि, meaning, the verb kriñ is annexed in the perfect tense, to verbs that take आम्. In this sûtra (III. 1. 40) the word kriñ is a pratyâhâra, implying the verbs भू and अस्. It might be asked how is this pratyâhâra formed? The word kri is taken from the fourth word of sûtra V. 4. 50, भूततद्भावे कृभ्वस्तियोगे &c. and the letter ñ is taken from sûtra V. 4. 58 कृञः सातिदाचिष्वलोपः &c. This is the way in which the commentators explain, how not only the verb kriñ is used as an auxiliary in forming the periphrastic perfect, but also the verbs भू and अस्. These three verbs denoting absolute action, unmodified by any especial condition, have in all languages been fixed upon as the best auxiliaries.

It must, however, be noted that the word kriñ in this sûtra is not used as a pratyâhâra and consequently does not include the verbs भू and अस्. Therefore कृ requires here Âtmanepada termination.

Thus एधाम् + कृ + त

Now applies the following :—

2241. The words 'eś' and 'irech' are the substitutes of 'ta' and 'jha' respectively in the Perfect tense.

The श् of एश् indicates that it replaces the whole of the affix त (I. 1. 55).

The च् of इरेच् is for the sake of accent (VI. 1. 165).

Thus एधे, एधाञ्चक्रे, एधाञ्चक्रिरे ।

Why are the substitutes taught here as एश् and इरेच् and not as ‹?› and ‹?›; for the would have become by III. 4. 79. § 2233? The very fact, that is uttered in these substitutes indicates by implication (jñâpaka) that the rule III. 4. 79, by which the of âtmanepada terminations are changed to , is not applicable to substitutes of Âtmanepada terminations. Therefore and which replace , and in are not governed by III. 4. 79, and is not changed to , nor to , nor to .

Thus एधाम् + कृ + त = एधाम् + कृ + ए . Now the लिट् affixes being ârdhadhâtuka, this requires that the should be gunated to . But this is prevented by the following :—

2242. The affixes of Liṭ (Perfect Tense) not coming after a conjunct consonant, are as if they had an indicatory क (kit).

The terminations of लिट् (Perfect) not being पित् terminations, are कित्, after verbs that have no compound consonants. The phrase अपित् (not being marked with प्) qualifies this sûtra also, being drawn from the previous Ashțâdhyâyî sûtra.
entries.note: Entry cut off at bottom of page 44; commentary continues on page 45.

entries.english:
Being the prohibition of I. 1. 5, S. 2217 applies and there is no guṇation, as otherwise would have been, by force of S. 2168.
Thus ‹?›. At this stage, two rules appear, one requiring the reduplication of ‹?› (लिटि धातोरनभ्यासस्य VI. 1. 8. S. 2177) and the other requiring ‹?› to be changed to ‹?› by इको यणचि (VI. 1. 77. S. 47). This last is subsequent in order of Ashṭâdhyâyî and therefore should take effect first. But if it took effect first, we have ‹?›. Then the reduplication will be ‹?›. Here no ‹?› is left for the application of VII. 4. 66 and we cannot get any form. Therefore ‹?› does not take place first, by the following.
entries.note: Continuation from page 44; begins mid-sentence.

entries.english:
2243. When an affix beginning with a vowel follows, that is a cause of reduplication, a substitute shall not take the place of a preceding vowel, whilst the reduplication is yet to be made; but the reduplication having been made, the substitution may then take place.

NOTE:—This sûtra has been explained in different ways by the authors of the Kâśikâ and of the Siddhânta Kaumudî. According to the former, the sûtra means:—Before an affix having an initial vowel, which causes reduplication, the substitute which takes the place of a vowel is like the original vowel even in form, only for the purposes of reduplication and no further. The explanation given by Kâśikâ is more in harmony with the Great Commentary. For all practical purposes, the two explanations lead to the same conclusion. According to Kâśikâ, the vowel-substitute is sthânivat, in the sense, that it is exactly of the same form as the original, and retains this form only for a fixed time viz., so long as the reduplication is being made; but as soon as the reduplication has been made, the substitute takes its proper form.

Thus in ‹?› is a vowel affix, and it causes reduplication; therefore substitution for the preceding vowel will not take place whilst the reduplication is to be made. Thus ‹?›. Now the following applies.

2244. A short ‹?› (I. 1. 51) is substituted for the ‹?› or ‹?› of the reduplicate when an affix follows.

The ‹?› is always followed by ‹?› by उरण् रपरः ॥ Thus we have ‹?›. The ‹?› is elided by हलादिः शेषः S. 2179.

Why do we say "when an affix follows"? Observe ‹?› (page 101 S. 199).

Why have we used the word "when the affix follows" in the sûtra? For would not the word ‹?› limit the designation to that only after which there was actually an affix?

Ans. No. Because without the word the sûtra would have run thus "after whatsoever is an affix enjoined, that which begins therewith is called an Aṅga." In this view, we could not get the form ‹?› in the perfect (लिट्) of the root ‹?› 'to cut.'

This is thus formed:—
‹?› = ‹?› (VI. 1. 8. लिटि धातोरनभ्यासस्य)
= ‹?› (VI. 1. 17. ‹?›)
= ‹?› (VII. 4. 66. उरत् and उरण् रपरः)
= ‹?› (VII. 4. 60. हलादिः शेषः) = ‹?› the 3rd per. Sing.

If the word "pratyaye" did not exist, then the designation aṅga would be applied to the whole base plus the affix i.e. (‹?›) as a whole. That being so, ‹?› will assume the form of ‹?› for the ‹?› will be vocalised by VI. 1. 17; for the ‹?› in the place of ‹?› will not be sthânivat, by अचः परस्मिन् पूर्वविधौ, because to be sthânivat, there must be an efficient cause outside (‹?›), as of ‹?›; but this ‹?› was by hypothesis included in the aṅga designation. So there being no outside cause, the substitute of ‹?› in ‹?› will not be sthânivat; and not being so, it will not be considered as a samprasâraṇa vowel. The ‹?› of ‹?› not being a samprasâraṇa, the prohibition (न संप्रसारणे संप्रसारणम् &c. VI. 1. 37) when a semi-vowel has once been vocalised, there is no vocalisation of the other semi-vowel that precedes it; will not apply, and so ‹?› will be vocalised to ‹?›.
entries.note: Text of English heading reconstructed where OCR lines were broken by inline Devanagari.

entries.english:
2245. For the Guttural and ह of a reduplicate there is substituted a Palatal.

Thus ‹?›. So also ‹?›.

Then we form 2nd. Pers. Sing. ‹?›.

Here the following sûtra prevents the insertion of इट् before थल्, which otherwise would have come by virtue of VII. 2. 35 S. 2184.

2246. The augment इट् is not added to that Ârdhadhâtuka affix, though beginning with a consonant except य, when it is joined to a root, which in the Grammatical system of Instruction (i.e. in the Dhâtupâṭha) is of one syllable, and is without accent (anudâtta).

The word upadeśe qualifies both words ekâc, and anudâtta. Why do we say "which is monosyllabic?" So that the present rule should not apply to the same root when it is Intensive, with the affix यङ् elided. The Intensive of every verb is included in the enunciation of its root; and as a general rule, all the sûtras specified for the simple root, will apply to the Intensive also, with certain exceptions, as contained in the following:—

शितपा शपानुबन्धेन निर्दिष्टं यद्गणेन च ।
यदेकाच् ग्रहणं चैव पञ्चैतानि न यङ्लुकि ॥

"These five sorts of operations will not apply to Intensive-yaṅ-luk forms:
1. When the simple root is exhibited in the sûtra with श्तिप् as भू in VII. 4. 73 is shown as भवति ॥ In the Intensive, the perfect will be बोभवाञ्चकार and not भवाञ्चकार. 2. Where the root is exhibited with श as the root ‹?› in VII. 2. 49 is shown as ‹?›. There is ‹?› after the Desiderative of simple root, but not in Intensive. 3. When a simple root is exhibited with an anubandha, as शीङ् VII. 1. 6. 4. Where a gaṇa is mentioned in a rule, as श्यन् is taught after Divâdi-roots (III. 1. 69). It will apply to simple roots of Divâdi gaṇa, and not to their Intensive. 5. Lastly, where the word एकाच् is used in a sûtra. As VII. 2. 10. That rule will apply to एकाच् simple roots and not to their Intensives.

This we infer because the word ekâc is used in the present sûtra. For had not this been the meaning, then there was no necessity of using the word "eka" in the sûtra, for the word अचः Abl. singular, by itself alone would have denoted one vowel; but by the additional use of the word "eka," the roots consisting of more than one vowel are excluded.
entries.note: Heading misprinted as 22.16; entry text cuts off at the end of page 47 and continues on page 48.

entries.english:
Therefore, since we find that the last statement in the above verse (‹?› &c.) is supported by the inference to be drawn from the present sutra, we may conclude that the other four statements of the above verse are also authoritative and approved by Panini. See also sûtra II. 2. 19.

Therefore the substitute root vadha (II. 4. 42) is not affected by the present rule; for though the root which replaces vadha in Dhatupatha is taught (upadesa) with one vowel, yet its substitute vadha is taught (upadesa) in the sutra II. 4. 42 with two vowels, hence it is not ekach: and so it gets the augment and we have vadhitum. But the prohibition applies to han as hantum and not hanitum.

The anudatta roots will be shown later on by giving a list of them.

Thus एधाम् + च + कृ + आ = एधाञ्चक्रे, and so also एधाञ्चक्राते ॥

The 2nd Pers. Pl. is एधाम् + चकृ + ध्वे

Here applies the next sûtra.

2247. The cerebral sound ‹?› is substituted in the room of the ध of षीध्वम्, and of the Personal-endings of the Aorist and the Perfect, after a stem ending in इण् (a vowel other than अ).

Therefore एधाम् + चकृ + ध्वे = एधाञ्चकृढ्वे ॥

एधाञ्चक्रे । एधाञ्चक्राते । एधाञ्चक्रिरे ॥

Similarly the perfect of एध् may be formed by the auxiliary भू as well as by अस्. But in the case of भू and अस्, though the Principal Verb is atmanepadi, the auxiliaries will be conjugated as Parasmaipadi. Thus एधाञ्चकार and एधामास &c. First person singular is एधाञ्चक्रे.

Now the perfect of अस् is formed by replacing अस् by भू; but here it is not so replaced, because then the rule about अस् being an auxiliary would be useless; as भू is already taught. Had it not been so, then instead of saying कृञ् चानुप्रयुज्यते &c., Panini would have used कृस चानुप्रयुज्यते or कृभूषानुप्रयुज्यते &c. But the fact that he uses the Pratyahara कृञ् shows that अस् must be conjugated as a distinct form, and not replaced by भू. Therefore though the Perfect of the Principal Verb is atmanepadi, yet the perfect of the Auxiliary Verb अस् is in parasmaipada. In other words, the forms आसाञ्चक्रे &c., can never stand alone, but must be used as auxiliaries. How is then अस् to be conjugated in the perfect? See below.

entries.english:
2248. A long vowel is substituted in the Perfect for the initial अ of a reduplicate.

This debars the single substitute of the form of the subsequent ordained by VI. 1. 97.

Thus अस् + णल् = आ + स् + णल् = आस ॥

Thus एधामासुः &c.

Singular Dual Plural

लुट् First Future.

The Periphrastic Future is regularly formed. Thus एध् + ता = एधिता ॥ So also एधितारौ, एधितारः, एधितासे, एधितासाथे । The second person plural is एध् + तास् + ध्वे

Here applies the following sûtra by which the स is elided.

2251. In the Imperative 'âm' is substituted for what would have substituted otherwise 'e' by III. 4. 79.

Thus एध + ते = एधताम् so also एधेताम् एधन्ताम् ॥ The 2nd person singular is एधसे ॥ Here applies the following, by which से is changed to स्व ॥

2252. For such an 'e' coming after 's' is substituted व, and for that coming after व is substituted अम् in the Imperative.

This supersedes the आम् substitution of the last sûtra. Thus for से we have एधस्व and for ध्वे we have ध्वम् ॥

Thus एध + से = एधस्व । एधेयाम् । एधध्वम् ॥ The 1st person singular is एध + इ Here by the following sûtra the इ is changed to ऐ

2253. The 'ai' is substituted for 'e' forming part of the affixes of the first person of the Imperative. This debars ‹?› of the preceding but one sûtra. Thus ‹?› = — एधै, एधावहै, एधामहै ॥ लोट् or Imperative. Singular. Dual. Plural. 1st person एधै एधावहै एधामहै 2nd person एधस्व एधेथाम् एधध्वम् 3rd person एधताम् एधेताम् एधन्ताम् -: 0 :- लङ् or Imperfect. Thus ‹?› + ‹?› + शप् + त ॥ Here the following sûtra causes the ‹?› to be replaced by ‹?›

entries.english: 2254. आट् acutely accented is the augment of a verbal stem beginning with a vowel, in the Aorist, Imperfect and the Conditional. This debars the augment अट् ॥ Thus आट् + एध् + त = ऐधत ॥ The vṛiddhi is by VI. 1. 90. S. 262. लङ् or Imperfect. Singular. Dual. Plural. 1st Person. ऐधे ऐधावहि ऐधामहि 2nd Person. ऐधथाः ऐधेथाम् ऐधध्वम् 3rd Person. ऐधत ऐधेताम् ऐधन्त -: 0 :- लिङ् or Potential. Thus एध् + शप् + त ॥ Now the next sûtra ordains the augment सीयुट् to ‹?›

2255. The personal endings of the Potential and the Benedictive take the augment 'sīyuṭ'. The ट् of सीयुट् is indicatory and shows that this augment is to be placed before the affixes (I. 1. 46 S. 38.) The उ is for the sake of pronunciation; this rule applies to the Ātmanepada affixes. In the Potential, the स of the augment is elided by VII. 2. 79. S. 2211. and the य् also, before a personal-ending beginning with a consonant, is dropped according to VI. 1. 66. S. 873. In the Benedictive, the augment retains its full form, only so far as it is not governed by VI. 1. 66. Thus एध् + सीयुट् + त = एध् + सीय् + त = एध् + ईय् + त (VII. 2. 79. S. 2211.) = एध् + ई + त (VI. 1. 66. S. 873) = एधेत ॥ So also एधेयाताम् ॥ The 3rd Person Plural is formed by the following.

2256. The affix 'ran' is the substitute of 'jha' in the 'Liṅ' (Potential and Benedictive). The झ in other places, is replaced generally by अन्त (VII. 1. 3. S. 2169.) but in लिङ्, it is replaced by रन् ॥ Thus एध् + ईय् + रन् = एधेरन् ॥ So also 2nd Person singular &c. are एधेथाः, एधेयाथाम्, एधेध्वम् ॥ The 1st Person singular is formed by the following.

2257. Short 'a' is the substitute of 'i' of the Ātmanepada first person singular in the Potential and Benedictive. Thus एध् + ईय् + अ = एध् + इय् + अ = एधेय ॥ So also एधेवहि, एधेमहि ॥ लिङ् or Potential. Singular. Dual. Plural. 1st Person एधेय एधेवहि एधेमहि 2nd Person एधेथाः एधेयाथाम् एधेध्वम् 3rd Person एधेत एधेयाताम् एधेरन् आशीर्लिङ् or Benedictive. In the Benedictive, the affixes are Ārdhadhātuka and hence the स of सीयुट् is not elided. The इट् and सीयुट् though not strictly affixes, are yet parts of affixes, and hence their स् is changed to ष् ॥ Thus एध् + इट् + सीयुट् + त = एध् + इ + षीय् + त् + त = एधिषीष्ट ॥ So also एधिषीयास्ताम् ॥ Benedictive or आशीर्लिङ्. The rule of intermediate I It has been already taught before, that as a general rule the augment इट् is added to all affixes which begin with a consonant except (VII. 2. 85. S. 2184.) These 102 roots ending in consonants are anudatta. The roots तृप् and दृप् are optionally, according to some authors, read in the Churâdi class. They are not to be taken here, but the Divâdi तृप् and दृप् and hence these are shown above with the vikarana श्यन् ॥ Moreover :— The roots स्विद्, ष्विद्, क्ष्विद्, ‹?› are also shown with the vikarana श्यन् ॥ The root पत् is shown with the vikarana शप् ; and the root सु with ‹?›. The भिद् root खिद् is Aniṭ (III. 12) i.e. खिद् 'to separate'. The खिद् of Rudhâdi takes इट्. (5.) Fifteen roots :— अद् 'to eat' [II. 1] अत्ता ; हद् 'to void excrement' (I. 1026) हत्ता ; स्कन्द् 'to leap' (I. 1028) स्कन्ता ; भिद् 'to break' (VII. 2) भेत्ता ; छिद् 'to cut' (VII. 3) छेत्ता ; क्षुद् 'to pound' (VII. 6) क्षोत्तान, क्षोत्स्यति ; शद् 'to perish' (I. 908, VI. 134) शत्ता ; सद् 'to sink' (I. 907, VI. 133) सत्ता ; स्विद् 'to sweat' (IV. 79) स्वेत्ता । The root स्विद् is exhibited as स्विद्यति in the kârikâ, showing that the Fourth class root is to be taken, and not the Bhuâdi (I. 780), which is udâtta and takes इट् ॥ पद् 'to go' (IV. 60), पत्ता ; खिद् 'to be troubled' (IV. 61, VI. 142, VII. 12) खेत्ता ; तुद् 'to strike' (VI. 1) तोत्ता ; णुद् 'to impel' (VI. 2) नोत्ता ; विद् (IV. 62) वेत्ता ॥ The root विद् is exhibited in the kârikâ, as विद्यति and विन्ते, therefore, the rule applies to दिवादि and रुधादि विद् ॥ The Adâdi (वेत्ति) and Tudâdi (विन्दति) विद् is सेट्, as वेदिता विज्ञानाय, वेदिता धनस्य ॥ (6.) Ten roots :— राध् with अप 'to offend' ; रुध् 'to obstruct' (IV. 65) रोद्धा ; युध् 'to fight' (IV. 64) योद्धा ; बन्ध् 'to bind' (I. 1022), बन्द्धा ; साध् 'to accomplish' (V. 17) साद्धा ; क्रुध् 'to be angry' (IV. 80) क्रोद्धा ; क्षुध् 'to be hungry' (IV. 81) क्षोत्धा ; शुध् 'to be pure' (IV. 82) शोद्धा ; बुध् 'to be aware' (IV. 63) बोद्धा ; व्यध् 'to pierce' (IV. 72) व्यद्धा ; सिध् 'to be accomplished' (IV. 83) सेद्धा । The roots शुध् and सिध् are exhibited in the Kârikâ with vikaraṇa (शुध्यति, सिध्यति) ; therefore शुध् and सिध् take इट् in other gaṇas than the Fourth ; as ‹?› and ‹?›. There is want of prohibition with regard to ‹?›, so we have सेधितव्यम् and सेधितोः ॥ राध् 'to accomplish' (IV. 71, V. 16) ; (7.) न्—Two roots : मन् 'to think' (IV. 67) मन्ता, हन् 'to kill' (II. 2), हन्ता ॥ The Divâdi should be taken, otherwise from मन्—मनिता (VIII. 9). (8.) प्—Thirteen roots : तप् 'to burn' (I. 1034, IV. 51) तप्ता तप्स्यति, तिप् 'to distil' (I. 885) तेप्ता ; आप् 'to obtain' (V. 14, X. 295) आप्ता ; वप् 'to sow' (I. 1052) वप्ता ; स्वप् 'to sleep' (II. 50) स्वप्ता ; लिप् 'to anoint' (VI. 139) लेप्ता ; लुप् (VI. 137) 'to break', The roots तृप् and दृप् optionally take इट्, as they belong to ‹?› class (VII. 2. 45, Divâdi 84-91). The special mention of these two roots in the kârikâ, is for the sake of indicating that these roots take ‹?› augment ; as त्रप्ता or तर्प्ता, or तर्पिता, दृप्ता, or दर्प्ता or दर्पिता ॥ The तृप् and दृप् belonging to the Tudâdi class, are Udâtta and सेट् ॥ सृप् (I. 1032) 'to creep' स्रप्ता ; शप् 'to curse' (I. 1049) शप्ता ; छुप 'to touch' (VI. 125) छोप्ता ; क्षिप् 'to throw' (IV. 14) क्षेप्ता ॥ (9.) भ्—Three roots : रभ् 'to desire' (I. 1028), as रब्धा, यभ् 'to coire' (I. 1020), यब्धा, लभ् 'to take' (I. 1024), लब्धा ॥ (10.) म्—Four roots : यम् 'to cease' (I. 1033), यन्ता ; रम् 'to play' (I. 908) रन्ता ; नम् 'to bow' (I. 887, 1030) नन्ता, गम् 'to go' (I. 1031) गन्ता ॥ (11.) श्—Ten roots :—दिश् 'to show' (VI. 3), दृश् 'to see' (I. 1037), दंश् 'to bite' (I. 1038), मृश् 'to rub' (VI. 131), स्पृश् 'to touch' (VI. 128), रिश् (VI. 126), रुश् (VI. 128) both meaning 'to hurt', क्रुश् (I. 909) 'to cry', विश् 'to enter' (VI. 130), लिश 'to be small' (IV. 70, VI. 127). As देष्टा, द्रष्टा, दंष्टा, म्रष्टा or मर्ष्टा, स्प्रष्टा or स्पर्ष्टा ॥ The roots with a penultimate short, which are anudâtta in the dhâtupâṭha, with the exception of ‹?› and ‹?›, take optionally the augment अम् (VI. 1. 59) ॥ रेश्टा, रोष्टा, क्रोष्टा, प्रवेष्टा, लेश्टा ॥ (12) Two roots : घस् 'to eat' (I. 747, and also substitute of अद्), as घस्ता ; वस् 'to dwell' (I. 1054), as वस्ता ॥ The वस् which takes Samprasâraṇa by VI. 1. 15 is meant here, and not वस् 'to cover' (II. 13), which does not vocalise, as वसित्वा वस्त्रेण, but उषित्वा from वस् 'to dwell' (VII. 2. 52). (13.) ष्—Ten roots : शिष् 'to distinguish' (VII. 14) शेष्टा ; पिष् 'to pound' (VII. 15) पेष्टा ; शुष् 'to become dry' (IV. 74) शोष्टा ; पुष् 'to be nourished' (IV. 73), पोष्टा ; त्विष् 'to shine' (I. 1050) त्वेष्टा ; विष् 'to pervade, to sprinkle' (I. 728, III. 13, IX. 51) वेष्टा ; श्लिष् 'to embrace' (I. 734, IV. 77) श्लेष्टा ; तुष् 'to be satisfied' (IV. 75) तोष्टा ; दुष् 'to be sinful' (IV. 76) दोष्टा दोषवति ; द्विष् 'to hate' (II. 3) द्वेष्टा, द्वेक्ष्यति ; कृष् 'to draw' (I. 1059, VI. 6 both Bhuâdi and Tudâdi are taken, as the kârikâ uses the two forms), क्रष्टा and कर्ष्टा ॥ (14.) Eight roots : दिह् 'to smear' (II. 5), देग्धा ; दुह् 'to milk' (II. 4), दोग्धा ; मिह् 'to sprinkle' (I. 1041) मेढा ; रुह् 'to grow' (I. 912) रोढा ; वह् 'to carry' (I. 1053) वोढा ; नह् 'to bind' (IV. 57) नद्धा ; दह् 'to burn' (I. 1041) दग्धा ; लिह् 'to lick' (II. 6) लेढा ॥ In other collections दृह् (I. 905, IV. 20), तृह् (IV. 89), स्निह् (VI. 23), ‹?›, are also enumerated; of these दृह् takes optionally इट् before affixes beginning with त, so also तृह् because it belongs to the ‹?› class (VII. 2. 45) the other two are not found (?) in root-collections hence the Kârikâ uses the words नह्यादयः ॥ We shall now conjugate all the roots of the Bhuâdi class, in their due order. We take the third root. 3. स्पर्ध 'to contend or vie with, to emulate, to compete.' Now we take up the conjugation of स्पर्ध्, the third root of Bhuâdi class. Its meaning given in the Dhâtupâṭha is "saṅgharṣa" which means "the desire to overcome another." This root is Intransitive, because the object is already included in the sense of the verb itself. It is Âtmanepadi. NOTE:—Thus it has been stated:— धातोरर्थान्तरे वृत्तेर्धात्वर्थेनोपसंग्रहात् । प्रसिद्ध्यविवक्षातः कर्मणोऽकर्मिका क्रिया ॥ लट् or Present Tense. स्पर्धते, स्पर्धेते, स्पर्धन्ते, स्पर्धसे, स्पर्धेथे, स्पर्धध्वे, स्पर्धे, स्पर्धावहे, स्पर्धामहे । लिट् or Perfect. स्पर्ध्+त=स्पर्ध्+ए (III. 4. 81. S. 2241) = स्पर्ध्+स्पर्ध्+ए Now applies the following sûtra :—

entries.english: अभ्यासस्य शर्पूर्वाः खयः शिष्यन्ते । 'हलादिः शेषः' (२१७९) इत्यस्यापवादः । पस्पर्धे । स्पर्धिता । स्पर्धिष्यते । स्पर्धताम् । अस्पर्धत । स्पर्धेत । स्पर्धिषीष्ट । अस्पर्धिष्ट । अस्पर्धिष्यत । गाधृ । प्रतिष्ठा-लिप्सयोर्ग्रन्थे च । गाधते । जगाधे । 'बाधृ ५ लोडने' । लोडनं प्रतिघातः । बाधते । 'नाथृ ६ याचनोपतापैश्वर्याशीःषु' । *आशिषि नाथ इति वाच्यम्* । अस्याशिष्येवात्मनेपदं स्यात् । नाथते । अन्यत्र नाथति । नापते । 'दध धारणे' । दधते । 2259. Of a reduplicate, the hard consonants (aspirate and unaspirate) when preceded by a sibilant, are only retained, the other consonants are elided. This is an exception to हलादिशेषः (S. 2179.) NOTE:—It should be said rather, a hard consonant preceded by a hard consonant or a sibilant is only retained and the खर् consonants are elided as in ‹?› here ‹?› becomes ‹?› by the augment ‹?› (तुक्) ; in the reduplicate then ‹?› should be elided, and ‹?› retained out of ‹?› ; and not ‹?› retained and ‹?› elided ; for the च् represents ‹?›, and if this were retained, it would be ‹?› and not ‹?› that would be heard : for by VIII. 2. 1, the change of ‹?› to ‹?› is asiddha for the purposes of this rule. Vârt:—The verb नाथ् when meaning 'to bless,' takes âtmanepada terminations, as, सर्पिषो नाथते 'blesses with clarified butter.' मधुनो नाथते । Why do we say when meaning to bless? Observe, माणवकमुपनाथति । Thus स्पर्ध् स्पर्ध् + ए = पस्पर्धे ; and so पस्पर्धाते, पस्पर्धिरे &c. लुट् or First Future 3. स्पर्धिता, स्पर्धितारौ, स्पर्धितारः, 2nd S. 1. &c.
