No peculiarity. Note: The indicatory ऋ is for VII. 4. 2. S. 2572 as लट् :— गाधते, गाधेते, गाधन्ते ॥ लिट् :— जगाधे ॥ लुट् :— गाधिता, गाधितारौ, गाधितारः ॥ लृट् — गाधिष्यते ॥ लोट् — गाधताम्, गाधस्व, गाधै ॥ लङ् — अगाधत, अगाधथाः, अगाधे ॥ विधिलिङ् — गाधेत, गाधेथाः, गाधेय ॥ आशीर्लिङ् — गाधिषीष्ट ॥ लुङ् — अगाधिष्ट, अगाधिष्ठाः, अगाधिषि ॥ लृङ् — अगाधिष्यत ॥ 5. बाधृ 'to harass, oppress, torment, press hard, annoy, trouble, disturb, vex, pain; 2. to resist, oppose, thwart, check, obstruct, arrest, interfere with. 3. to roll (लोडने) 4. to tempt. (विलोभने)' The word लोडन means to resist, or re-act. लट् :— बाधते ; लिट् :— बबाधे &c. Note :— From this root is derived the noun बाहु: "hand." By adding the Uṇâdi affix कु (u), and changing ध to ह (I. 27.) 6. णाथृ (नाथ), 7. णाधृ (नाध) 'to ask, beg, to solicit for anything, 2. to be sick, to harass, to trouble; 3. to have power, to be master, to prevail 4. to bless.' These roots are Âtmanepadî when meaning "to bless" and not when meaning “to ask" &c. (II. 3. 55 S. 616). लट् :— नाथते “he blesses" or नाथति “he begs” &c. Note:— उपताप means 'disease' (रोग) ; another reading is उपघात (Tarangini). Both these roots begin with a dental न. When meaning 'to bless,' it takes Âtmanepada, and the noun in construction is put in the sixth case by II. 3. 55. S. 616. As सर्पिषो नाथनम् । The sixth case affix is not elided in the compound. So we cannot have the form सर्पिर्नाथनम् । For here we have pratipada-vidhânâ sixth case. But when it is krid yoga shashṭhî, then there is compounding. When it does not mean 'to bless,' we have Parasmaipada. As, लट् — नाथति ; लिट् — ननाथ ; लुट् — नाशिता ; लृट् — नाशिष्यति ; लोट् — नाथतु ; लङ् — अनाथत् ; विधिलिङ् — नाथेत् ; आशीर्लिङ् — नाथ्यात्, अनाथीत् ; लृङ् — अनाशिष्यत् । Note: Maitreya and Âbharaṇakâra read the first root as णाट्; and they have the form प्रणाटते । On this Kâśyapa says "णाथते नोपदेवत्वनपुष्टं, गणरत्नमहोदधिवृत्तिकारादीनामनभिमतात्" ॥ 8. दध “1. to hold, 2. to have, possess, 3. to give, present.” लट् :— दधते, दधेते, दधन्ते ; दधसे ; दधावहे, दधामहे । लिट् = दध् + ए = ददध् + ए । Now apply the following sutras :-

entries.english: 2260. ए is substituted for the short अ standing between two simple consonants of a verbal stem, before the personal endings of the Perfect which have an indicatory क् (I. 2. 5), provided that, at the beginning of the root, in the reduplication, no different consonant has been substituted; and when this ए is substituted, the reduplicate is elided.
entries.note: Sutra serial number misprinted as 2230 in source, corrected to 2260.

entries.english: 2261. ए is substituted for अ, of a verbal stem standing between two simple consonants, the stem not having any different letter substituted in the reduplicate, when the ending थल् of the Perfect having the augment इट् follows, and thereby, the reduplicate is elided. By the phrase "no other consonant has been substituted" is meant "no other dissimilar in form consonant has been substituted". This we learn from the implication (jñâpaka) of sûtra VI. 4. 126 where exception is made in the case of ‹?› and ‹?›. Therefore, where the substitute is a different letter, then the reduplicate becomes âdeśâdi: otherwise not. If the form of the letter is not changed in the reduplicate, by substitution, then such substitution will not make the stem âdeśâdi. Thus by VIII. 4. 54, a letter (ग्, घ्, ड्, etc.) is substituted for a consonant (other than a nasal and a semi-vowel) in the reduplicate. Thus in the reduplicate is ‹?›, the first is also a substitute, for the substitute of ‹?› will be ‹?›. Such substitutes, however, are not meant here. Here, therefore, there will be the elision of the reduplicate and the ए substitution. Thus Similarly द + दध् + ए = देधे ॥ So also, 3. d. देधाते ; 3. p. देधिरे ; देधिषे, देथे, देधिवहे ॥ So also रेजतुः, रेजुः, येनतुः, येनुः, पेचतुः, पेचुः, देभतुः, देभुः ॥ Why 'for short अ'? Observe दिदिवतुः, दिदिवुः the इ is not replaced. Why do we say 'short अ'? Observe रासतुः, रासुः... Why do we say 'standing between two simple consonants'? Observe तस्तरतुः, तस्तरुः. Some say this example is not appropriate, for by I. 2. 5, the Perfect affixes are not कित् here, as they come after a conjunct consonant. The following is then more appropriate: सस्मरतुः ; and शशमतुः (Bhu. 586). Why do we say 'which has no substitute consonant in the reduplicate'? Observe चकाणतुः, चकाणुः, जघ्नतुः, जघ्नुः, बभूवतुः, बभूवुः ॥ The substitution referred to here must be caused by the affixes of the Perfect, therefore, the rule will apply to ‹?› and ‹?› though ‹?› and ‹?› are the roots, and ‹?› and ‹?› are changed to ‹?› and ‹?›. The substitution of a consonant or a consonant in the reduplicate, should not be here considered asiddha (VIII. 2. 54, read with VIII. 2. 1.). That substitution will be considered a substitution for the purposes of this sûtra and will make the stem, as is indicated by the special exception made in favor of ‹?› and ‹?› in sûtra VI. 4. 122. 8 दध लट् — दधते, दधेते, दधन्ते ; दधसे ; दधावहे, दधामहे । लिट् — देधे, देधाते, देधिरे ; देधिषे ; देथे, देधिवहे लुट् — दधिता, दधितारौ, दधितारः । लृट् — दधिष्यते । लोट् — दधताम्, दधस्व, दधै ॥

9. स्कुदि “to jump, to raise or lift.” The i in स्कुदि is indicatory and by the following न् is inserted.
Note :—According to Tarangini, the root means, 1. आप्लवनम्, or 2. उत्प्लवनम् or 3. उदयनम् ॥ According to Bhoja, it means उद्धरणम् also.

2262. न् is added after the vowel of the root, in a root which has an indicatory इ in the Dhatupatha.

Thus स्कुन्द + शप् + ते = स्कुन्दते, स्कुन्दसे, स्कुन्दे ॥ Perfect :—पुस्कुन्दे, पुस्कुन्दषे, पुस्कुन्दध्वे । लुट्—स्कुन्दिता । लृट्—स्कुन्दिष्यते ॥ लोट्—स्कुन्दताम् ॥ लङ्—अस्कुन्दत । विधिलिङ्—स्कुन्देत ॥ आशीर्लिङ्—स्कुन्दिषीष्ट ॥ लुङ्—अस्कुन्दिष्ट ॥ लृङ्—अस्कुन्दिष्यत ।

10. विदि “to become white.” It is an Intransitive verb. Thus Pres. विन्दते ; Per. विविन्दे ॥

11. वदि “to salute, to praise, to worship.” Pres. वन्दते, Per. ववन्दे ; लुट् वन्दिता &c.
Note :—प्रह्वतिपूर्वभाषणं is अभिवादनम् । Noun वन्दः = पूजकः ॥

12. भदि “to tell a good news, to be fortunate, to be glad, to honor, to shine.” Pres. भन्दते, Per. बभन्दे, लुट्—भन्दिता &c.
Note:—Noun भद्र “auspicious,” भद्रा “shaving.”

13. नदि 'to praise, to rejoice, be glad, to be drunk, or be proud, to sleep or be lazy, to shine, to move (slowly),' मदे 'to be languid,' and जये 'to be victorious.' It is Intransitive except when meaning 'to praise' or 'to move.'
Pres. नन्दते, Per. ननन्दे ॥ लुट् नन्दिता ॥ Nouns :—नन्दथुः ; नन्दनः, नन्दी, नन्दा ।

14. स्पदि “to throb, vibrate.” It is Intransitive.
Pres. स्पन्दते, Per. पस्पन्दे (VII. 4. 61 §. 2259); लुट् स्पन्दिता ॥ Nouns :—स्पन्दः, स्पन्दनः ॥

15. क्लिदि “to grieve, lament.” This is a Transitive verb. Pres. क्लिन्दते चैत्रम् 'he laments for Chaitra.' Per. चिक्लिन्दे ॥

16. मुद “to rejoice.” Pres. मोदते ॥ Per. मुमुदे । No guna because of (I. 2. 5).
मोदते, मोदसे, मोदे ।
लिट्—मुमुदे, मुमुदाते, मुमुदिषे, मुमुदिध्वे ॥
लुट्—मोदिता ॥ लृट्—मोदिष्यते ॥ लोट्—मोदताम् ।
लङ्—अमोदत । विधिलिङ्—मोदेत ॥ आशीर्लिङ्—मोदिषीष्ट ॥
लुङ्—अमोदिष्ट ॥ लृङ्—अमोदिष्यत ॥
Nouns :—मोदनः ; मोदः ; मोदिरः ; मोदमानः ; मोदा ।

17. दद 'to give, present.' Pres. ददते, Per. देदे — But this is a wrong form, as the following sutra applies.

entries.english:
2263. ए is not substituted for the अ of शस्, दद्, or of roots beginning with व्, or of such verbal stems in which the अ results through the substitution of Guna, though the affixes of the Perfect being कित् or ङित् follow, or the set थल्, nor is the reduplicate elided.

Thus (विशशसतुः, विशशसुः, विशशसिथ) दददे, दददाते, दददिरे ॥ लट् । ददते, ददेते, ददन्ते ॥ लिट्—दददे, दददाते, दददिरे, दददिषे ॥ लुट् ददिता । लृट् ददिष्यते ॥ लोट् ददताम् ॥ लङ् अददत । विधिलिङ् ददेत ॥ आशीर्लिङ् ददिषीष्ट । लुङ् अददिष्ट ॥ लृङ् अददिष्यत ॥
(Of roots beginning with व् :— ववनतुः, ववतुः, ववनिथ ॥ Of roots where अ is the result of guna, विववरतुः, विववरुः, विववरिथ, लुलविथ, पोपथिथ ॥ गुणशब्देन निर्वृत्तस्यात एवेह ग्रहणान्न तु सवर्णदीर्घे कृत आकारस्य चायमकार इति रत्वं प्रतिषिध्यते ॥)
The अ of Guna may result either from the guna of ऋ changed to अर्, or of उ changed to ओ again changed to अव् as—लव ॥

18. ष्वद, 19 ष्वर्द “to taste, to be liked, be sweet, be pleasant to the taste; to sweeten.” This root is Transitive when meaning “to experience” i. e. to taste, and it is Intransitive when meaning “liking” i. e. to be liked. According to Kshiraswami it means “to choose.” Transitive; as स्वदतेऽन्नम् 'he tastes food' ॥ It is Parasmaipadi here as a Vaidic Irregularity. Intransitive, as स्वदते सर्पिर्देवदत्ताय “curd is pleasant to the taste of Devadatta.”
It is conjugated regularly. The initial ष् in ष्वद् is changed to स् by the following :—

entries.english:
2264. There is the substitution of स् in the room of the ष्, being the initial of a verbal root as enunciated in the Dhatupatha.

Therefore ष्वद् is changed to स्वद्, and this is not again changed to ष्, because of the prohibition of sutra VIII. 3. 111. §. 2128. Thus अनुस्वदते ।
लिट् :—तस्वदे ॥ Similarly स्वर्दते, तस्वर्दे ॥ Generally the root स्वद is preceded by the upasarga आ, as आस्वदते ‹?› ।

20. ऊर्द 'to measure, to play.' By force of च 'and,' this root also means 'to taste.' According to Sanmati, the word मान does not mean 'measure' but for happiness, and “to be cheerful or easy.”

Thus ऊर्द + शप् + ते ॥ Here applies the following sutra.

entries.english:
2265. The short इ or उ of a root is lengthened, when the verb has र् or व् as its penultimate letter, and is followed by a consonant.

* The anuvritti of दीर्घः is current from the preceding Ashtadhyayi sutra.
The root must end in a consonant, and must have र् or व् as preceding such consonant, for the application of this rule.

Therefore the उ is lengthened. Thus we have.
ऊर्दते ; लिट् :—ऊर्दाञ्चक्रे । लुट् ऊर्दिता । लृट् ऊर्दिष्यते । लोट् ऊर्दताम् । लङ्—और्दत । विधिलिङ्—ऊर्देत । आशीर्लिङ्—ऊर्दिषीष्ट । लुङ्—और्दिष्ट । लृङ्—और्दिष्यत ॥

21. कूर्द, 22. खूर्द, 23. गूर्द, 24. गुद । In Kaiyyata, Purushakara and Maitreya the root ‹?› is not found. In Sanmati, Amogha, Vistara and Chandra all the first three roots are given. In Charaka ‹?› is taken as one word meaning 'free.' But according to Maitreya and Kasyapa, ‹?› is a separate root. So all the four roots mean "to play." The force of च here implies that roots have numerous meanings, but here one meaning alone is to be taken, namely "to play."

Thus कूर्दते, चकूर्दे ; खूर्दते ; गूर्दते ; गुदते, जुगुदे ॥

In future the words लट् &c. will often be omitted. It is to be understood that the words are arranged in that order. As, 1. कूर्दते, 2. चकूर्दे ; 3. कूर्दिता, 4. कूर्दिष्यते ; 5. कूर्दताम् ; 6. अकूर्दत, 7. कूर्देत, 8. कूर्दिषीष्ट, 9. अकूर्दिष्ट, 10. अकूर्दिष्यत ॥

25. षूदँ "to flow, effuse, pour out, distil." It is an Intransitive verb in these senses. When meaning 'to strike, hurt, wound, kill, destroy,' it is Transitive, as formed by घञ् of III. 1. 134. S. 2896. The causative has the additional sense of "to cook, dress, season, prepare." As सूदयति (संस्करोति) । So also अहोरात्राणि नस्तो विलिष्टं सूदन्तु (= द्राढं कुर्वन्तु) । Thus सूदते, Per. सुषूदे, ॥ लुट् = सूदिता । Noun सूद: "a cook, a morass."

NOTE:—Why do we say 'initial' in the preceding sutra 2264? Observe— कर्षति, कृषति ॥ Why have these roots been exhibited in the Dhatupatha with an initial ष, when for all practical purposes this ष is to be replaced by स, would it not have been easier to spell at once these words with a स? This appears cumbersome no doubt, but the spelling of the roots with ष is for the sake of brevity. Certain roots change their स into ष when preceded by certain letters: those roots which thus change their letter for ष have been at once taught with an initial ष, and thus by VIII. 3. 59 their स is changed to ष. Thus from षिच् instead of ‹?› we have ‹?› । This root is exhibited in the Dhatupatha with a ष, and thus we know that the स must be changed to ष. Otherwise a list of such roots would have to be separately given. One must refer to the Dhatupatha for a list of the roots beginning with ष ; As a general rule, however, all monosyllabic roots beginning with a स and followed by a vowel or a dental letter have been taught in the Dhatupatha as beginning with an initial ष, as well as the following roots, ‹?›, ‹?›, ‹?›, and ‹?› though followed by ‹?› or ‹?›. The following roots though followed by a vowel or dental are not taught with an initial ष viz. ‹?›, ‹?›, ‹?›, ‹?›, ‹?›, ‹?› ॥

The "dental" here means the dental pure and simple. i. e. त, थ, द, ध, न and not dento-labial व । This we infer from the inclusion of स्वद &c. in the list, which are followed by व । Had व been included in the terms "dental" there was no necessity of teaching स्वद &c. separately.

NOTE :—To complete the description of verbs, we shall anticipate matter and give under each root its various derivative roots also, such as the Passive stem, the Causative (णिच्), the Desiderative (सन्), the Intensive with यङ् and the Intensive without यङ्, (यङ् लुगन्त); as well as some Krit derivatives where necessary. In this we have followed the Madhaviya Dhatuvritti. We repeat therefore, the conjugation of the twenty five roots already taught.

अत १८ सातत्यगमने । अतति । 'अत आदेः' (२२४८) आत । आतुः । आतुः । अतिता, अतिषिष्यति इत्यादि न विशेषः ॥

38. √ Aṭa, 'to go constantly, to wander.' The words mean 'an uninterrupted going.' As ग्राममतति 'He wanders throughout the village.'

Thus, Pre. अतति, अततः, अतन्ति । Per. आत, आतुः, आतुः । अतिथ, आतिथ । The a is lengthened by VII. 4. 70. S. 2248. I Fut. अतिता । II Fut. अतिषिष्यति । Imp. अततु । There is Vṛiddhi before the augment āṭ. Pot. अतेत् । Bene. अत्यात् ।

In forming the Aorist, we add sic and īṭ. Thus a + āt + sic + īṭ + t. The sic is the affix of the Aorist and is added by III. 1. 44 S. 2222. The augment iṭ is added to this sic by VII. 2. 35 S. 2184. The personal ending gets the augment īṭ by VII. 3. 96, S. 2225. So the equation stands thus: ātiṣ + s + īt ॥

Now applies the following sūtra by which the s is elided.
entries.note: Continuation from page 74; contains reprinted Aniṭ-kārikās and introductory discussion on root 38 preceding SK 2266.

entries.english:
2266. The s is dropped after the augment iṭ, if after this s the augment īṭ follows.

Thus āt + iṣ + s + īt = āt + i + 0 + īt.

Now this s is elided by VIII. 2. 28 (the present sūtra) of the Tripādī (the last three sections or Pādas of the Aṣṭādhyāyī).

This elision would, therefore, be asiddha for the purposes of ekādeśa (VI. 1. 101 S. 85), and we could not combine the i of iṣ with the long ī as the zero intervenes. So the form would be ‹?› as in case of sūtra VIII. 3. 19 S. 67; for VIII. 2. 1 S. 12 applies. To prevent this anomaly, we have the following vārtika:—

Vārt:— When ekādeśa is to be done, the elision of sic is to be considered siddha or valid. As आतीत् । Here the sic is elided by ईटि (VIII. 2. 28). This elision is considered valid or siddha, and thus we have dīrgha single substitution of ī for i + 0 + ī in āt + i + 0 + īt = आतीत् ॥

This elision of s takes place when it is situated between iṣ on one side and īṭ on the other. When there is not īṭ following, there is no elision. आतीष्टाम्, अतिषुः ।

The above examples आतीत्, आतीष्टाम् and अतिषुः may be either with or without a. The question is what is the true form of the Aorist without the augment a; is it अतीत् or आतीत्? According to the next sūtra it might have been आतीत्, but that sūtra is set aside by the sūtra following it.

2267. In the Parasmaipada s-Aorist there is Vṛiddhi of the a of vad, and vraj, and of any vowel, without distinction, of the stems ending in a consonant.

Note:— As, अवादीत्, आव्राजीत् । This debars the option in the case of these two roots, which would have otherwise obtained by VII. 2. 7. So also of stems ending in consonants: as अयाक्षीत्, अभैत्सीत्, अच्छैत्सीत्, अरोत्सीत् ॥

The root अत is a हलन्त root and therefore, there would be Vṛiddhi of अ into आ. But the application of this sūtra is prevented by the following sūtra:—
entries.note: Devanagari heading number and Panini reference digits partially corrupted/dropped in OCR.

entries.english:
2268. The vowel of a stem, ending in a consonant, does not get Vṛiddhi, when the sic takes the augment iṭ.

Therefore we do not get the form आतीत्, but अतीत्; because the sic here takes the augment iṭ.

Thus without the augment we have the forms: मा भवानतीत् or मा भवान् अतिष्ट, मा भवान् अतिषुः । The augment a is elided after mā. The form is therefore really a + atīt and not a + ātīt.

Pre. अतति । Per. आत, आतुः, आतुः, अतिथ । I Fut. अतिता । II Fut. अतिषिष्यति । Imp. अततु । Imper. आतत् । Pot. अतेत् । Bene. अत्यात् । Aorist अतीत्, अतिष्टाम्, अतिषुः (without a). Condi. अतिष्यत् ।

Pass. Per. आते । I Fut. अतिता । II Fut. अतिषिष्यते । Imp. अतात । Imper. आतत । Pot. अतेत । Bene. s. अतिषीष्ट, d. अतिषीयास्ताम्, pl. अतिषीरन् । Caus. आतयति । Desi. अतिचिषति । Past. Part. Pass. अतितः । Nouns: आतिः 'a kind of bird', पत्तिः 'infantry', अश्विनी 'an asterism', अतिथिः 'a guest', अनिलः 'air', पतत्त्री 'bird'.

चिती ३९ संज्ञाने । विचेष्टितः ॥

39. √ Chiti, 'to perceive, see, notice, observe', 'to know', 'to understand', 'to remember'; 'to think'.

Pre. — चेतति । Per. चिचेत, चिचिततुः, चिचितुः ; चिचेतिथ, चिचिथ, चिचितथुः, चिचित । I Fut. चेतिता । II Fut. चेतिष्यति । Imp. चेततु । Imper. अचेतत् । Pot. चेतेत् । Bene. चित्यात् । Aor. अचेतीत्, अचेतिष्टाम्, अचेतिषुः । Condi. अचेतिष्यत् । Caus. चेतयति, Aor. अचीचितत् । Desi. चिचेतिषति or चिचितिषति
entries.note: Text cuts off at the bottom of page 77 mid-entry during root 39; verb paradigm OCR heavily corrupted.

entries.english:
Inten. चेकेत्यते । Yan luk चेकेतीति or चेकेत्ति । Past Part. चित्तः, चित्तवान् । Ger. चित्त्वा or चेतित्वा । Nouns चेतनः, चित्, चेतः, चेतन्ती, चैतन्यम् ॥

च्युतिर् ४० आसेचने । सेचनमार्द्रीकरणम् । आङीषदर्थेऽभिव्याप्तौ च ॥
* इरित्संज्ञा वाच्या * । श्च्योतति । चुश्च्योत ॥

40. √ Chyutir, to sprinkle. सेचन means to sprinkle, to wet. The prefix आङ् has the force of 'a little,' or 'pervasion.' आसेचन therefore means to wet a little or 'to wet thoroughly.'

Vartika:—The whole portion इर् whenever it occurs at the end of a root is to be treated as इत् । Thus Pre. श्च्योतति । Per. चुश्च्योत ॥

As this root has an indicatory ‹?›, the effect of it is that in the Aorist, it has another form also, where च्लि is replaced by अङ् and there is consequently no guna. The Sutra which causes this is the following:—
entries.note: Tail continuation of SK 2268 from preceding page.

entries.english:
2269. अङ् is optionally the substitute of च्लि after that root which has an indicatory इर्, when the Parasmaipada terminations are employed.

NOTE:—Thus from छिदिर् (छिद्) 'to divide,' we derive, अच्छिदत्, or with सिच् अच्छैत्सीत् । But we have अच्छित्त in the Atmanepada. So from भिदिर्—अभिदत्, or अभैत्सीत् ।

Similarly च्युतिर्, has its Aorist either as अच्योतीत्, or अच्युतत्, with अङ् affix.

40. √ Chyutir, to sprinkle, to wet. Pre.—श्च्योतति । Per. चुश्च्योत । च्योतति । चुच्योति । I Fut. श्च्योतिता । II Fut. श्च्योतिष्यति । Imp. अश्च्योतत् । Pot. श्च्योतेत् । Bene. श्च्युत्यात् । Aorist अच्युतत्, or अच्योतीत् । Pass. श्च्युत्यते । Caus. श्च्योतयति । Aor. अचुश्च्योतत् । Desi. चुश्च्योतिषति or चुश्च्युतिषति । Inten. चोश्च्युत्यते । Yan luk चोश्च्योतीति or चोश्च्योत्ति । Past Part. Pass. श्च्युतितः or श्च्योतितः । Ger. श्च्योतित्वा ।

41. √ Schyutir, 'to trickle, ooze, exude, flow;' 'to shed, pour out, diffuse, scatter.' Pre. श्च्योतति । Per. चुश्च्योत &c. like च्युत् । Aor. अच्युतत्, with अङ्, or अच्योतीत् ॥

Some read this root without स्, namely as च्युतिर् । Then the conjugation will be च्योतति &c. As in मधुश्च्युतं घृतमिव सुपूतम् ॥

NOTE:—The whole portion इर् is indicatory, and not इ and र् separately. They can be made separately also by उपदेशेऽजनुनासिक इत् (I. 3. 2. S. 3); which will make इ indicatory; and by हलन्त्यम् (I. 3. 3. S. 1) which will make र् indicatory. This is done actually by Madhava in his Dhatuvritti. But the objection to it is that if र् be taken separately as indicatory, then there should be an insertion of nasal by इदितो नुम् धातोः (VII. 1. 58. S. ‹?›).

42. [भासने 'to shine'].
Similarly should be conjugated the root ‹?› । This root is not given in the Siddhanta.

43. Mantha, 'to churn,' to agitate, shake, stir round or up, to crush, to grind down, oppress, afflict, destroy, kill. Pre. मन्थति । Per. ममन्थ, ममन्थिथ । I Fut. मन्थिना । II Fut. मन्थिष्यति । Imp. अमन्थत् । Imper. अमन्थत् । Pot. मन्येत् । Bene. मथ्यात् ॥

In the Benedictive, the n of मन्थ is elided, because the affix यासुट् is कित् by III. 4. 104 S. 2216; and because it is कित् it causes the elision of न् by VI. 4. 24 S. 415. Had the root been read as मथि, there would have been no elision of the nasal. In fact, there is such a root also, as given below. See Root 47.

Aor. अमन्थीत् । Cond. अमन्यिष्यत् । Passive मध्यते । Causative मन्धयति । Aor. अममन्थत् । Desiderative मिमन्थिषति । Inten. मामथ्यते । Yan luk मामन्थीति or मामन्ति । Imperfect अमामन् । Gerund मथित्वा or मन्धित्वा । Nouns:—मन्थः, मन्थनी ॥

This root takes two accusatives, as सुधां क्षीरनिधिं मथ्नाति ॥

44 √ Kuthi, 45 √ Puthi, 46 √ Luthi, 47 √ Mathi, 'to hurt, to suffer pain, to injure, to strike, to kill, to be afflicted, to crush, to grind down, to oppress.' Pre. कुन्थति । Per. चुकुन्थ &c. like मन्थ as given above. In the Benedictive (आशीर्लिङ्) however, there will be no elision of the nasal. As कुन्ध्यात् ; पुन्ध्यात् &c.

Similarly लुन्थति, पुन्थति and मन्थति । Both roots मथि and मन्थ are read here, according to Saumata. Kshiraswami reads it समन्थे and not मथि even here, and gives the example मन्थ्नाति । All these roots mean 'to injure.' As शत्रुमभिकुन्थति, मारयति ॥

48. √ Shidha, 'to go, to ward, to drive.' Some read this with an indicatory short उ । The initial ष् is changed to स् by धात्वादेः षः सः (VI. 1. 64 S. 2264). Pre. सेधति । Per. सिषेध, सिषिधिथ; सिषेधिथ । I Fut. सेधिता । II Fut. सेधिष्यति । Imp. असेधत् । Pot. सेधेत् । Ben. सिध्यात् । Aor. असेधीत् । Cond. असेधिष्यत् ।

Passive सिध्यते । Causative Pre. सेधयति, Aor. असीषिधत् । Desiderative सिषिधिषति or सिषेधिषति । Intensive सेषिध्यते । Yan luk सेषेधीति or सेषेत्ति । Gerund सेधित्वा or सिधित्वा । Nouns सेधः 'a kind of tree,' सिद्धम् and सिद्धयन्तः ।

When an upasarga like नि is added we have नि+सेधति । The question arises should स् be changed to ष after नि ? The Sutra VIII. 3. 111, S. 2125 requires that there should be no substitution, since सेधति is the beginning of a Pada. To this, however, the following sutra makes an exception. That sutra (VIII. 3. 65) and the five sutras that follow it in the order of Ashtadhyayi are given together here once for all, to show when स् should be changed to ष, not only in the case of षिध् but of other verbs also:

Thus नि+षेधति=निषेधति (see below).
entries.note: Contains embedded root discussions (Roots 40-48) spanning pages 78-80 before next sutra.

entries.english:
2270. ष is substituted for स, after an alterant इ and उ of an upasarga in the following verbs: षु (सुनोति), सू (सुवति), सो (स्यति VII. 3. 71), स्तु (स्तौति VII. 3. 89), स्तुभ् (स्तोभते), स्था, सेनय (Denominative), सिध् (सेधति), सिच्, सञ्ज् and स्वञ्ज् ॥

Thus सुषोति । सुषाव, प्रसुषाव । स्यति, अभिष्यति । स्तु, अभिष्टौति । स्तुभ्, अभिष्टोभते । स्था, अभिष्ठास्यति । सेनय, अभिषेणयति । सेध, अभिषेधति, परिषेधति, पर्यषेधत् । सिच्, अभिषिञ्चति । सञ्ज्, अभिषजति । स्वञ्ज्, परिष्वजते ॥

NOTE:—The root सिध् is exhibited in the sutra as सेध with vikarana, thus debarring षिधु—सिध्यति ॥

2271. The स of ष्वष्क is changed to ष after an Upasarga having an इ or उ, but not after प्रति ॥

Thus परिष्यष्कति, प्रणिष्यष्कति, निषष्वाष्क, सुष्वष्क । The second ष् remains unchanged in the Perfect by VIII. 3. 118.

Why do we say 'but not after प्रति' ? Observe प्रतिष्वष्कति ॥
entries.note: Heading misprinted in original text as 2871 for 2271.
Entry begins at bottom of page 80 with sutra line and Sanskrit vritti fragment; English translation cut off.

entries.english: 2272. The s of स्तम्भ (read in sutra III. 1. 82 S. 2555.) is changed into ष after an upasarga, having an i or u. Thus अभिष्टम्भाति । परिष्टम्भाति । The word अप्रतेः of the last sûtra is not to be read here. Hence we have forms like:— प्रतिष्टम्भाति । ‹?› । ‹?› The present sûtra is made a separate rule, when it could well have been included in the immediately preceding one, as सदिस्तम्भोः for two reasons. First that the anuvritti of स्तम्भ alone should run into the next sûtra. Secondly that it should not be restricted by the word अप्रतेः । प्रतिष्टम्भनः ॥
entries.note: Sutra line missing from scan (printed on preceding page in letterpress original).

entries.english:
2273. The स् of स्तम्भ is changed into ष after the preposition अव in the sense of 'support' and 'contiguity.'
Note:—The word 'आलम्बन' means 'support, refuge, that upon which anything depends or leans,' 'अविदूर' means 'the state of not being दूर or far off, i.e. to be contiguous.'
Thus अवष्टभ्यास्ते 'He remains leaning upon a staff &c.,' अवष्टभ्य तिष्ठति ।
So also in the sense of to be near, as अवष्टब्धा सेना 'the army near at hand,' ‹?› । See V. 2. 13.
अवष्टभ्यास्ते—मित्वा सन् समीपे चास्ते ॥

2274. The ष is substituted for the स of स्वन्, after वि and अव, when the sense is 'to smack while eating.'
Thus विष्टनति, विष्टणति, विष्टनायते, अवष्टनति, अवष्टणति, अवष्टनायते । That is, he makes sound while eating, he eats with a smack.

2275. [ष] is substituted for the स of सेव्, सित, सय, सिवु, सह, the augment सुट्, स्तु and स्वञ्ज्, after the prepositions परि, नि, and वि.
Thus निषेधति । The root षेवृ 'to serve' belongs to the Bhvâdi class. The सित is the Past Participle of षिञ् बन्धने, and सय is the noun derived from the same root with the affix अच्; सिवु is a Divâdi root.
Note:—The root सित of this rule is an important landmark. All roots enumerated in the sutras VIII. 3. 65 to VIII. 3. 70 change their स to ष even when the augment अट् intervenes, but not so the root सित and those that follow it. This is taught in the next sûtra.

2276. (The substitution of ष, for स्, as taught hereinbefore will take place) for all roots up to सित exclusive in VIII. 3. 70 even when the augment अट् intervenes (between the स and the alterant letter).
This sûtra governs all the fifteen roots given in the preceding sutras from VIII. 3. 65. Thus with the augment अट् we have न्यषेधत् in the Imperfect, न्यषेधीत् in the Aorist and न्यषेधिष्यत् in the Conditional.

2277. In स्या &c. up to सित exclusive (VIII. 3. 65 to VIII. 3. 70), this ष substitution takes place then also, when the reduplicate intervenes, and the स of the reduplicate is also changed to ष.
Thus सिषेध, सिषिधतुः in the Perfect.

2278. The स् of the verb षेध is not changed to ष when the meaning is that of moving.
This is an exception to VIII. 3. 65 S. 2270. Thus गङ्गां विसेधति ।
षिधू ४९ शास्त्रे माङ्गल्ये च । शास्त्रं शासनम् ।
49. Şhidha, 'To ordain, command, instruct,' 'to turn out well or auspiciously'. शास्त्र means command, rule. This root has an indicatory long ऊ, the force of which is given in the next sûtra. It is conjugated like the preceding root ‹?› No. 48 except in so far as the effect of the indicatory ऊ makes the change.
लुट्—सेधिता । लृट्—सेधिष्यति ।
In the 2nd Person Dual we have सिषिधथुः with the augment इट् added to थुस्.
But this augment is optional, owing to the root having an indicatory ऊ as given below.
entries.note: Entry text includes Dhatupatha root 49 commentary and paradigm spanning pages 82-83.

entries.english:
2279. A Valâdi-Ârdhadhâtuka affix optionally takes 'iṭ' after svṛi, after the two roots 'sû' (sûti and sûyati), after 'dhûñ' and after a root which has an indicatory long 'û'.
Thus सिषेध् + थ । Now applies the next sûtra.

2280. 'Dha' is substituted for 'ta' or 'tha' coming after 'jha', 'bha', 'gha', 'ḍha' or 'dha' (jhash), but not after the root dhâ (dadh).
Note:—Thus from लभ्, we have लब्धा, लब्धुम्, लब्धव्यम्, अलब्ध, अलप्सत ॥
Thus सिषेध् + थ = सिषेध् + ध = सिषेद्ध । The other form is सिषेधिथ । सिषिधतुः or सिषिध्यतुः । लुट्—सेधिता or सोद्धा । लृट्—सेधिष्यति or सेत्स्यति । लोट्—सेधतु । लुङ्—असैत्सीत् ।
In the 3rd Person Dual we have असेध् + स् + ताम् । Now applies the next sûtra, which causes the elision of स् ॥

2281. The 's' is elided when it is preceded by a jhal consonant (any consonant except semi-vowels and nasals), and is followed by an affix beginning with a jhal consonant.
Thus असेध् + स् + ताम् = असेद्धाम् ॥
Therefore the full conjugation in Aorist is:—
Singular Dual Plural.
Third Person असेत्सीत् असेद्धाम् असेत्सुः
Second Person असेत्सीः असेद्धम् असेद्ध
First Person असेत्सम् असेत्स्व असेत्स्म
Second Form.
Third Person असेधीत् असेधिष्टाम् असेधिषुः
Second Person असेधीः असेधिष्टम् असेधिष्ट
First Person असेधिषम् असेधिष्व असेधिष्म
The Desiderative is सिषेधिषति ॥
50. 'to eat. The ‹?› is indicatory.
51.
entries.note: Entry text cut off at bottom of batch (page 83); Aorist paradigm table reconstructed from OCR fragments.

entries.english: The force of the indicatory ‹?› is that we have no shortening of the penultimate in ‹?› ॥ Desiderative : चिखादिषति । Intensive : चाखाद्यते । Yaṅ-luk चाखादीति or ‹?› । Causative : खादयति । Past Participle खादितः । Noun खादकः ॥ 51. खद् 'to be steady, firm,' 'to strike, hurt, kill.' By the force of the word 'and,' it means 'to eat' also. It is Intransitive when meaning 'to be firm,' — लट्—खदति । लिट्—चखाद । Here we have caused the Vṛiddhi of the अ of खद् by the following sūtra.
entries.note: Tail continuation from page 83.

entries.english: 2282. In a stem ending in a consonant with an 'a' immediately preceding it, the Vṛiddhi is substituted for such 'a' when an affix having an indicatory 'ñ' or 'ṇ' follows. Therefore खद् + णल् = चखाद ॥ In the First Person singular, however, this Vṛiddhi is optional by the next sūtra.

2283. The ending of the First Person Singular in the Perfect optionally acts as ṇit. The Vṛiddhi is optional, as चखाद or चखद ॥ The other Tenses are conjugated like खाद । In the Aorist (लुङ्) there are two forms caused by the following :—

2284. SUB SECTION 4.
Note:— The author of the Dhatupatha commenced his book with the root एध् ending in a dental, because that root had an auspicious meaning. Vart:— The affixes of the Perfect are kit after roots that have a penultimate ऋ; and even the subsequent rule of Guna is superseded in the case of these. By I. 2. 5, S. 2242 the affixes of Lit are kit after roots that do not end in a conjunct consonant. Thus विद = विविदुः । विविदिषुः । Here the kitva is nitya, and guna is anitya. But in ववृके both the kitva and the guna are anitya; therefore guna being taught subsequent to kitva would take effect. This is prevented by the present vartika by purva-vipratishedha.

entries.english:
2290. इयङ् and उवङ् are substituted for the इ and उ of a reduplicate, before a non-homogenous vowel.
Therefore उ+ओख+अ = उव्+ओख+अ = उवोख । When by Guṇa, the root assumes the form ओख्, it becomes a heavy vowelled root : and the Perfect ought to be formed by the addition of आम् periphrastically by III. 1. 36 S. 2237 but this is not so because of the maxim संनिपात &c. ("that which is taught in a rule the application of which is occasioned by the combination of two things, does not become the cause of the destruction of that combination." See VII. 1. 9 S. 203). Here उ was changed to ओ by the presence of णल्; and if आम् be added, it will cause the elision of its progenitor अच् by II. 4. 81 S. 2238 which the maxim prevents.
The dual is formed thus उख+उख+अतुस् = उ+उख+अतुस् = ऊखतुः । The Plural is ऊखुः । The affixes being कित्, there is no guṇa, and consequently no उवङ् substitution, as the vowels are now homogenous. This single substitute long ऊ (उ+उ=ऊ) may be considered as the final of the first or the beginning of the second (VI. 1. 85. S. 75). Considering it as final of the first, namely, as the long of the reduplicate (abhyāsa), it requires to be shortened by VII. 4. 59. S. 2180.
[But because the rule of shortening depends upon abhyāsa alone and is therefore antaraṅga, while the savarṇa-lengthening is Bahiraṅga ; as it depends upon two, namely the precedent and the subsequent letters— the maxim "नाजानन्तर्ये बहिष्ट्वप्रक्लृप्तिः" applies (see Vol I. p. 30) : and so it is not shortened. Or].

entries.english:
It is not shortened, because it had already been once shortened before, and "an operation once performed on a stem &c., is not repeated again"—is the maxim that would apply.

Note:—When was the first u shortened? It was shortened by VII. 4. 59, S. 2180 as soon as was reduplicated to उ + उ । But it was already short, how could it be shortened?

Ans. Rules of grammar act like clouds (which rain both on sea and on land though raining on sea is useless). The rule of ह्रस्वः S. 2180 therefore substitutes a short in the place of the already existing short उ. Thus उ + उख + अतुः = उ + उख + अतुः (VII. 4. 59 S. 2180) =

But why should Rule S. 2180 apply first and not the rule of lengthening? In other words, why should we not make उ + उख = ऊख first and then apply the rule of shortening?

The rule of shortening being a rule applicable to anga (or stem) is stronger than the rule of lengthening (अकः सवर्णे दीर्घः) on the maxim:

Paribhasha: A rule relating to a stem (anga) is stronger than a rule relating to letters.

Therefore, the ह्रस्वः (S. 2180) applies first.

Another reason for its applying first is that it is subsequent in order to the rule of lengthening.

Thus उ + उ + ख् + अतुः = उ + उख + अतुः (S. 2180 short for short उ) = ऊखतुः (lengthening). Similarly कख् : कखतुः ॥

SUB-SECTION VI.

Now we take up the roots ending in ch. There are twenty one Atmanepadi roots.

चर्च १७५ दीप्तौ । चर्चते ॥

175. चर्च 'To shine.' लट्—चर्चते । लिट्—चचर्चे । लुट्—चर्चिता । लृट्—चर्चिष्यते । लोट्—चर्चताम् । लङ्—अचर्चत । विधिलिङ्—चर्चेत । आशीर्लिङ्—चर्चिषीष्ट । लुङ्—अचर्चिष्ट । लृङ्—अचर्चिष्यत । Caus. चर्चयति । Aor. अचचर्चत् । Des. चिचर्चिषते । Inten. चाचर्च्यते । Yan luk. चाचर्कीति or चाचर्ति । Aor. अचाचर्कीत्, अचाचर्त् ॥ Noun चर्चः 'vigour,' 'faeces.' ब्रह्मवर्चसम् । Adjective चर्च्यम् ॥

176. सच 'to sprinkle, to serve.' लट्—सचते । लिट्—सेचे । लुट्—सचिता । लृट्—सचिष्यते । लोट्—सचताम् । लङ्—असचत । विधिलिङ्—सचेत । आशीर्लिङ्—सचिषीष्ट । लुङ्—असचिष्ट । Caus. सचयति । Aor. अससचत् । Des. सिषाधयिषते (VIII. 3. 61. S. 2627). Yan. सासच्यते । Yan luk. सासक्ति । Noun सक्तुः । सक्तुकः । सचिवः ॥

लोच १७७ दर्शने । लोचते । लुलोचे ॥

177. दर्शने To see. लोचते । लुलोचे । लोचिता । Des. लुलोचिषते । Inten. लोलोच्यते, लोलोचीति, लोलोक्ति ॥ Caus. लोचयति । Aor. अलुलोचत् ॥

178. व्यक्तायां वाचि to speak distinctly. शेचे । शचिता । N. शची ॥

त्वच १७९ श्वचि १८० गतौ । त्वचते ।

179. त्वच \ गतौ To go. त्वचते । चत्वचे । त्वचिता । N. त्वक् ॥
180. श्वचि / श्वञ्चते । शश्वञ्चे । श्वञ्चिता ॥

कच १८१ बन्धने । कचते ॥

181. कच 'to bind.' कचते । चकचे । कचिता । N. कचः, कचाः ॥

कच १८२, काचि १८३, दीप्तिबन्धनयोः । कञ्चते । चकाचे ॥

182. कच \ दीप्तिबन्धनयोः to shine, to bind. कञ्चते । चकचे । कचिता ।
183. काचि / काञ्चते । चकाञ्चे &c. Nouns : कञ्चुकः । काञ्ची । काञ्चनम् ।

मच १८४, मुचि १८५, कल्कने । कल्कनं दम्भः शाठ्यं च । कात्थनम् इत्यन्ये । मञ्चते । मुमुञ्चे ॥

184. मच \ कल्कने to cheat, to be vain. Some say it means to brag or boast
185. मुचि / also. Thus मञ्चते । मेचे । मचिता । मुञ्चते । मुमुञ्चे । मुञ्चिता । According to Chandra the root is मोच—मोचते ॥

ऋजू १८९ गतिस्थानार्जनोपार्जनेषु । भर्जते । नुट्-विधावकारेरेफयोरेकहलत्वेन ज्ञेयम् । तेन द्विहलत्वादिट् । आनृजे ॥

189. ऋजू । To go. 2. stand or be firm, strong, earn or obtain or get. Maitreya gives the meaning of वर्जन also.
लट्—ऋर्जते । लिट्—आनृजे । ऋज् + ऋज् + ए = ऋ + ऋज् + ए (VII. 4. 60. S. 2179) = अर् + ऋज् + ए (VII. 4. 66 S. 2344 read with I. 1. 51). The अ is then elided by VII. 4. 60, S. 2179 and we have आ + [ अ ] + र्ज् + ए = आर्ज् + ए + नुट् (The lengthening by VII. 4. 70. S. 2248, and नुट् by VII. 4. 71. S. 2288) = आनर्जे ॥ For the purposes of adding नुट्, the ऋ is considered to have र् in it so that ऋज् becomes equivalent to र्ज्, so the root is considered to be one which ends in a double-consonant, and thus makes S. 2288 applicable. लुट्—अर्जिता । अर्जिष्यते । लोट्—ऋर्जताम् । लङ्—आर्जत । आशीर्लिङ्—अर्जिषीष्ट । लुङ्—आर्जिष्ट । Inten. अरार्यते । Caus. अर्जयति । Aor. आर्जिजत् । Des. अर्जिजिषते । Gerund अर्जित्वा । Adjective अर्ज्यम् ॥

आजि १९०, भृञी १९१ भर्जने ।
'उपसर्गादृति—' (९४) इति वृद्धिः । प्राजते । प्राञ्चे । प्रानिष्ट । भर्जते । बभ्रज्जे ॥

190 आजि, 191 भृञी । To parch. The root भृञ् has a long ऋ as indicatory.
प्र + आजते = प्राजते, with प्र, the vriddhi is by VI. 1. 91. S. 74. लिट्—प्राञ्चे । Or प्रावृञ्चे according to Sammata and Tarangini. But this is wrong. नुट् लट्—भर्जते । लिट्—बभ्रज्जे ।

The following seventy-two roots up to √ vraj are Parasmaipadi.

entries.english: verbs 'to grow old' स्तम्भ 'to stiffen' म्रुच् and म्लुच् 'to go' ग्रुच् and ग्लुच् 'to steal,' ग्लुञ्च 'to go' and 'to grow', when the terminations of the Parasmaipada are employed. Thus अम्रुचत् or अम्रोचीत् 'he went' ; अम्लुचत् or अम्लोचीत् 'he went'. The roots ग्रुञ्च् and ग्लुञ्च् both give rise to the same three forms, viz. अग्रुचत्, अग्रोचीत् and अग्लुचीत्. The use of one root, would, therefore, have served the purpose. The employment of both indicates separateness of their meanings. Others say that the use of both roots indicates that in the case of ग्लुञ्च, the nasal is never elided. Thus the Aorist of ग्लुञ्च will be अग्लुञ्चत् and अग्लुञ्चीत्. म्रुचु २१२, ग्लुचु २१३, कुजु २१४, खुजु २१५, स्तेयकरणे । म्रोचति । अम्रुचत् अम्रोचीत् । जुम्लोच । अम्लुचत्—अम्लोचीत् । अकोजीत् । अखोजीत् ॥ 212. √ Gruchu, 213 √ Gluchu, 214 √ Kuju, 215 √ Khuju 'to steal'. लट्—म्रोचति । लिट्—जुम्रोच । लुट्—म्रोचिता । लुङ्—अम्रुचत् or अम्रोचीत् । Noun म्रोकः, म्लोकः ॥ 213. √ Gluchu 'to steal.' लट्—म्लोचति । लिट्—जुम्लोच । लुङ्—अम्लुचत् or अम्लोचीत् ॥ 214. √ Kuju 'to steal.' लट्—कोजति । लुङ्—अकोजीत् ॥ 215. √ Khuju 'to steal.' लट्—खोजति । लुङ्—अखोजीत् ॥ ग्लुञ्च २१६, षस्ज २१७, गतौ । अङ् । अग्लुचत्—अग्लुञ्चीत् । षस्य शत्वेन शः, जश्त्वेन जः । सज्जति । अयमात्मनेपद्यपि । सज्जते ॥ 216. Ishti:—The substitution is optional before ârdhadhâtukas beginning with a letter of Pratyâhâra val (all consonants except y). As ‹?›

In viyatuḥ and viyuḥ the ‹?› is changed to ‹?› before atuḥ and us. The equation now stands thus viy + atuḥ. Here the root has a penultimate letter य which is followed by a consonant; therefore the i of viy ought to be lengthened by VIII. 2. 78 S. 2265. But it is not so, because the y, substitute for ‹?›, is considered sthânivat to ‹?›, by I. 1. 51, S. 50, for the purposes of S. 2265. y being as ‹?›, the penultimate is not considered to be followed by a consonant but by a vowel, and hence S. 2265 cannot apply. Obj.:—But the rule VIII. 2. 78, S. 2265 is a dīrgha-vidhi, as it ordains lengthening and therefore the substitute of ‹?› will not be sthânivat by I. 1. 51. S. 50; because that rule must be read with the proviso of I. 1. 58 S. 51 which declares inter alia that for the purposes of dīrgha-vidhi the âdeśa is not sthânivat, so there ought to be lengthening of viy.

Ans:—The following vârttika makes a counter-exception to that rule of S. 51.

Vârt:—For the application of the rules of accent (svara-vidhi), or the rules of lengthening (dīrgha-vidhi) or the rule of the elision of ya (ya-lopa-vidhi), the lopa-substitute only of a vowel is to be considered as not sthânivat, and not any other substitute. Here the substitute is y and not lopa; and so is considered sthânivat to ‹?›.

In forming the Second Person Singular, we have aj + thal = vi + â + thal = ‹?›. Now applies the prohibition of S. 2246 debarring the augment इट्. But the following sûtra makes an exception.

entries.english:
2293. The Personal endings of the Perfect do not get the augment इट् after कृ, सृ, भृ, वृ, स्तु, द्रु, स्रु, श्रु ॥

The four roots, कृ, सृ, भृ, and वृ are taken in order to make a restriction with regard to them. Every prohibition of इट् augment whether depending on any particular final, or depending on any particular affix, if that prohibition is to apply to the Perfect, then it applies only to the four roots kṛ &c. mentioned here, and not to other roots.

As regards the remaining four roots स्तु, द्रु, स्रु, and श्रु, the present sûtra prohibits the इट् which would have come before the affix थल् by the rule of Bhâradvâja (VII. 2. 63 S. 2296) and the इट् which would have come before the affixes व or म &c. by the present rule of Krâdi (i.e., the affixes व, म, महिङ् and महिङ्);

Note:—Thus कृ—चक्रे, चक्रिवहे; चकृमहे; भू—बभूव, बभूविव &c. ‹?›

These roots with the exception of ‹?› are Aniṭ by VII. 2. 10 S. 2243; their special mention here is for the sake of niyama, namely these roots alone are aniṭ in the Perfect, other roots are all Seṭ in the Perfect. Thus ‹?› All anudâtta roots of the Dhâtupâṭha are to be understood, by this rule, to get इट्. The affix थल् of the Perfect gets इट् after भू, as the irregular form बभूविथ in VII. 2. 64, indicates that in the Vedic it does not get इट् after भू, but in the classical literature it does. By VII. 2. 63, S. 2296 the थल् would have got इट् after द्रु and स्रु; that also is prohibited by the present sûtra. As तुष्टोथ, दुद्रोथ, सुस्रोथ, शुश्रोथ ॥

Vârt:—इट् is added when कृ takes the सुट् augment: as संचस्करिथ, संचस्करिम । The sûtra VII. 2. 63, S. 2296 applies here also, as संस्करिथ ॥

2294. After a root, which in the Dhâtupâṭha, ends in a vowel, and after which the First Fut. affix tâsi is always devoid of the augment इट्; (after such a root) थल् the personal ending of the Perfect, like tâsi, does not also get the augment इट् ॥
entries.note: Panini reference digits in OCR read 7.2.13 (misprint or misread for 7.2.61).

entries.english: 2295. After a root which possesses a short 'a' as its root vowel in the original enunciation (the Dhâtupâṭha), and after which the First Fut. affix तासि is always devoid of the augment इट्, थल् the Personal ending of the Perfect, like तासि, does not get the augment इट् ॥
entries.note: Panini reference digits in OCR read 2.2.62 (misread for 7.2.62).

entries.english:
2296. In the opinion of Bharadvaja, it is only after a root which ends in a short ऋ, and after which the First Fut. तासि is always devoid of the augment इट् that थल् also, like तासि, does not take the augment इट्.

Therefore, the other affixes do take इट्. On this there is the following verse (saṅgraha), which sums up the last three sûtras:—

That root which ends in a vowel, or which has a short अ in the Dhâtupâṭha, and which is aniṭ before तास् affix, is optionally सेट् before थल् affix. But if such root ends in short ऋ, then it is invariably aniṭ before थल् affix. Roots other than कृ &c. are सेट् in the Perfect.

One should not, however, think that the four roots स्तु, द्रु, स्रु and श्रु will also be optionally aniṭ in थल् as they are not ṛi-ending roots. The rule made by Bharadvâja removes the prohibition with regard to the addition of इट् made by the two immediately preceding sûtras S. 2294 and 2295 : and not the इट् of S. 2293. This is on the maxim 'a rule, may it enjoin or forbid anything, either enjoins or forbids only that which is nearest to it in some other rule.' (see Vol I. 203)

Therefore वि + अ + आज् + थ = विवजिथ or विव्यजिथ or विव्याजिथ ।

entries.english: लट् - हेठते । लिट् - जिहेठे । लुट् - हेठिता । णिच् - हेठयति । Aor. अचीहिठत् । एठि २८६ च । एठाञ्चक्रे ॥ 286. ✓ eṭhi. It has the same meaning as ‹?› According to Svâmi and Kâśyapa it is always preceded by वि । But Maitreya and others give examples without वि ॥ लट् - एठते । लिट् - एठाञ्चक्रे । लुट् - एठिता । णिच् - एठयति । Aor. मा भवान् टिठत् । The shortening takes place prior to reduplication. सन् - टिट्ठिषते ॥ हिडि २८७ गत्यनादरयोः । हिण्डते । जिहिण्डे ॥ 287. ✓ hiḍi, To go, to disregard, slight. लट् - हिण्डते । लिट् - जिहिण्डे । लुट् - हिण्डिता । णिच् - Aor. अजिहिण्डत् । सन् - जिहिण्डिषते । यङ् - जेहिण्ड्यते । Yaṅ-luk - जेहिण्डीति । Imperfect - अजेहिन् ॥ हुडि २८८ संघाते । जुहुण्डे ॥ 288. ✓ huḍi, To collect. Kâśyapa says “The Âryas do not read this root. But the Drâviḍas read it.” लट् - हुण्डते । लिट् - जुहुण्डे । लुट् - हुण्डिता ॥ कुडि २८९ दाहे । चुकुण्डे ॥ 289. ✓ kuḍi, to burn. लट् - कुण्डते । लिट् - चुकुण्डे । लुट् - कुण्डिता । Nouns :— कुण्डः । कुण्डी । कुण्डा । कुण्डम् ॥ वडि २९० विभाजने । मडि २९१ च ॥ ववण्डे ॥ 290. ✓ vaḍi, 291. ✓ maḍi. To share out, distribute, divide. According to Svâmi the root maḍi being made a separate sûtra has other meanings also. But Nandi reads these sûtras वडि विभाजने and मडि वेष्टने । लट् - वण्डते । लिट् - ववण्डे । ममण्डे । लुट् - वण्डिता । मण्डिता । Noun - मण्डपः ॥ भडि २९२ परिभाषणे । परिहासः सनिन्दोपालम्भश्च परिभाषणम् । बभण्डे ॥ 292. ✓ bhaḍi. Deva says परिहासे । Svâmi and others say that paribhâshaṇa means to proclaim, shout. According to Amarakośa, ridiculing one with censure is paribhâshaṇa. लट् - भण्डते । लिट् - बभण्डे । Noun भण्डारः 'ambassador.' पिडि २९३ संघाते । पिपिण्डे ॥ 293. ✓ piḍi, to collect. लट् - पिण्डते । लिट् - पिपिण्डे । Noun पिपिण्डकः 'a boy.' मुडि २९४ मार्जने । मार्जनं शुद्धिन्यग्भावश्च । मुण्डते ॥ 294. ✓ muḍi. to rub over, to cleanse ; to sink. लट् - मुण्डते ॥ तुडि २९५ तोदने । तोदनं दारणं हिंसनं च । तुण्डते ॥ 295. ✓ tuḍi. To break, to kill. Todana means 'to split,' 'to injure.' लट् - तुण्डते । Nouns तुण्डिः । तुण्डिलः । तुण्डिभः ॥ हुडि २९६ वरणे । वरणं स्वीकारः । 'हरणे' इत्येके । हुण्डते ॥ 296. ✓ huḍi, to choose. Varaṇa means selection. Maitreya says it means haraṇa also, i. e., seizing. Another reading is ✓ Bhuḍi, bharaṇe (to support). लट् - हुण्डते । स्फुडि २९७ विकसने । चडि २९८ कोपे । चण्डते ॥ 297. ✓ sphuḍi to open, expand. This root is not in the Siddhânta. 298. ✓ chaḍi, to grow angry. लट् - चण्डते । Nouns :— चण्डः । चण्डी ॥ शडि २९९ रुजायां संघाते च । शण्डते ॥ 299. ✓ śaḍi to wound and to collect. लट् - शण्डते । Nouns शण्डः । शण्डिलः ॥ तडि ३०० ताडने । तण्डते ॥ 300. ✓ taḍi to strike, to thresh. लट् - तण्डते । Nouns तण्डः । वितण्डा तण्डुलः ॥ पडि ३०१ गतौ । पण्डते ॥ 301. ✓ paḍi, to go, move. लट् - पण्डते । Nouns पण्डितः । पण्डः । पण्डारकः ॥ कडि ३०२ मदे । कण्डते ॥ 302. ✓ kaḍi, to be intoxicated. लट् - कण्डते ॥ खडि ३०३ मन्थे । 303. ✓ khaḍi, to churn. लट् - खण्डते । Noun खण्डः ॥ हेड ३०४, होड ३०५ अनादरे । जिहेडे । जुहोडे ॥ 304. ✓ heḍṛ, 305. ✓ hoḍṛ. To disregard. Heḍṛ in the sense of veshṭhana is ghaṭâdi. Hoḍṛ to go is Parasmaipadî. Pre. - हेडते । होडते । Per. - जिहेडे । जुहोडे । 1 Fut. - हेडिता । Caus. - हेडयति । Aor. - अजिहिडत् । Des. - जिहेडिषते । Inten. - जेहेड्यते । Yaṅ-luk - जेहोडीति । Noun - होडः ॥ बाड ३०६ आप्लाव्ये । घटादिः । आप्लाव्यमाप्लवः । बाडते ॥ 306. ✓ bâḍṛ, to dive, emerge, to bathe. The root begins with a b. Some read it with व v. Âplâvya has the same meaning as âplava i. e. bathing. Pre. - बाडते ॥ द्राड ३०७, ध्राड ३०८ विशरणे । द्राडते । ध्राडते ॥ 307. ✓ drâḍṛ, 308. ✓ dhrâḍṛ, to cut, to divide. Pre. - द्राडते । ध्राडते ॥ शाड ३०९ श्लाघायाम् । 309. ✓ śâḍṛ, to applaud, praise, boast. According to Kâśyapa the root is शाल, the ल and ड being interchangeable letters. Pre. - शाडते । Nouns शाडा 'saloon,' शाडीनः 'modest.' Here end the Âtmanepadî roots whose final is a lingual. SUBSECTION VIII. अथ टवर्गान्ताः परस्मैपदिनः Now all the lingual ending roots are Parasmaipadis. शौट ३१० गर्वे । शौटति । शुशौट ॥ 310. ✓ śauṭṛ. To be proud or haughty. Pre. - शौटति । Per. - शुशौट । 1 Fut. - शौटिता । II Fut. - शौटिष्यति । Caus. - शौटयति । Aor. - अशूशौटत् । Desi. - शुशौटिषति । Inten. - शोशौट्यते । Yaṅ-luk - शोशौट्टीति । The reduplicate is first shortened and then guṇated. Impers. - शौटतु । Imperf. - अशौटत् । Pot. - शौटेत् । Bene. - शौट्यात् । Aor. - अशौटीत् ॥ यौट ३११ बन्धे । यौटति ॥ 311. ✓ yauṭṛ to join together. Pre. - यौटति ॥ म्लेट ३१२, म्रेड ३१३, मेट ३१४, उन्मादे । द्वितीयो डान्तः । टान्तमध्ये पाठस्त्वर्थसाम्याच्चार्थातिवत् । म्लेति । म्रेडति ॥ 312. ✓ Mleṭṛ, 313. ✓ Mreḍṛ, 314. ✓ Meṭṛ 'to be mad.' The second root ends in ड, its being read here along with roots ending in ट is because it has the same meaning as म्लेट्. Just as नर्द was read with नाथ. This root meṭṛ is not given in the Siddhânta. Pre. - म्लेति । म्रेडति ॥ कट ३१५ वर्षावरणयोः । 'चट ३१६' इत्येके । चकाट । सिचि 'अतो हलादेर्लघोः' (२२८४) इति वृद्धौ प्राप्तायाम् ॥ 315. ✓ kaṭa, 316. ✓ chaṭa, 'to rain,' 'to screen,' 'to cover.' Pre. - कटति । चटति । Perf. - चकाट । चचाट । Aor. - अकाटीत् । अचाटीत् ॥ Nouns :— कुठः । निकटः । कटरम् 'leather' । कटुः 'bitter.' चाटुः 'flatterer.' चटुलः । चटकः ॥ The two roots are marked with an indicatory ॠ and therefore in forming their aorist, the following Sûtra S. 2299 applies in supersession of S. 2284.

entries.english: 2299. The Vṛiddhi of the vowel of the following stems does not take place before the इट्-augmented s-Aorist in the Parasmaipada ; namely—the stems ending in ह्, म् or य्, the roots क्षण, श्वस् and जागृ, a stem formed with णि, the root श्वि, and the roots having an indicatory ॠ in the Dhâtupâṭha. Note:—Thus ग्रह, 'to catch' अग्रहीत् ; श्यम्, 'to sound' अशमीत् । वम्, 'to vomit' अवमीत् । व्यय, 'to expend' अव्ययीत् । क्षण, 'to hurt' अक्षणीत् । श्वस्, 'to breathe' अण्वसीत् । जागृ, 'to be awake' अजागरीत् । णि, ऊन (churâdi), 'to lessen' अनवीत् ; ईष, 'to send' ऐषीत् ॥ श्वि, अश्रयीत् । ॠदिताम्, कट, 'to cover' अकाटीत्, अचाटीत् ॥ Therefore there is no Vṛiddhi. Thus we have अकाटीत् and अचाटीत् ॥ अट ३१७, पट ३१८ गतौ । आट । आटतुः । आटुः । पपाट । पेटतुः । पेतुः ॥ 317. ✓ Aṭa, 318. ✓ paṭa 'to go, to wander, to roam.' Pre. - अटति । Per. - आट । आटतुः । 3. entries.english:
329. ✓ Bhaṭa, to nourish, to hire, to receive wages. This root is also found in the Ghaṭādi list in the sense of 'to proclaim'.
Pre. भटति । Per. बभाट । I Fut. भटिता । Aor. अभाटीत्, अभटीत् । Caus. भाटयति । Desi. बिभटिषति ॥

330. ✓ Taṭa, to groan, to rise or be raised.
Pre. तटति । Per. तताट । I Fut. तटिता । Aor. अताटीत्, अतटीत् । Nouns — तटी । तटिनी ॥

331. ✓ Khaṭa, to desire, wish.
Pre. खटति । Per. चखाट । I Fut. खटिता । Aor. अखाटीत् or अखटीत् । Caus. खाटयति । Desi. चिखटिषति । Inten. चङ्खट्यते । Noun : खट्वा ॥

332. ✓ Naṭa, to act on the stage. This root begins with ण so that we have प्रणटति । There is another root नट taught with न as नाटि । That belongs to the Churādi class.
Pre. नटति । Per. ननाट । I Fut. नटिता । Aorist अनाटीत्, अनटीत् । Caus. नाटयति or नाटयति । Desi. निनटिषति । Inten. नानट्यते । Nouns : नटी, नाट्यम् ॥

333. ✓ Piṭa, 1. to sound, 2. to heap or collect together.
Pre. पेटति । Per. पिपेट । I Fut. पेटिता । Aorist अपेटीत् । Caus. पेटयति । Aorist अपीपिटत् । Desi. पिपेटिषति or पिपिटिषति । Inten. पेपिट्यते । Nouns : पिटकम्, पिटः । Gerund : पेटित्वा or पिटित्वा ॥

334. ✓ Haṭa, to shine, be bright.
Pre. हटति । Per. जहाट । I Fut. हाटिता । Aorist अहाटीत् or अहटीत् । Caus. हाटयति । Desi. जिहटिषति । Inten. जाहट्यते । Noun हाटक 'gold'.

Pre. षटति । Perf. सषाट । षेटतुः । I Fut. षटिता । Aorist असाटीत्, अषटीत् । Caus. साटयति । Aorist असीषटत् । Desi. सिषटिषति (The स is not changed to ष because of VIII. 3. 61 § 2627) Inten. साषट्यते । Noun : सटा ॥

336. ✓ Luṭa, to suffer pain. Some say this root ends in ड. Others make it end in त, as in Magha 'लोलद् भुजाकारबृहत्तरङ्गम्' । This is found in the Divādi class also.
Pre. लोटति । Perf. लुलोट । I Fut. लोटिता । Aorist अलोटीत् । Caus. लोटयति । Aorist अलुलुटत् or अलोटत् । Desi. लुलोटिषति or लुलुटिषति । Inten. लोलुट्यते । Past Part. Pass. लुटितः । Past Part. Act. लुटितवान् । Ger. लोटित्वा or लुटित्वा ॥

337. ✓ Chiṭa, to send forth or out.
Pre. चेटति । Per. चिचेट । चिचिटतुः । चिचिदुः । I Fut. चेटिता । Aorist अचेटीत् । अचेदिष्टाम्, अचेदिषुः । Caus. चेटयति । Desi. चिचेटिषति or चिचिटिषति । Inten. चेचिट्यते । यङ् लुक् चेचिटीति or चेचेत्ति । Gerund चेटित्वा or चिटित्वा । Noun चेटी ॥

338. ✓ Viṭa to sound.
Pre. वेटति । Per. विवेट, विविटतुः, विविदुः । I Fut. वेटिता । Aor. अवेटीत् । Caus. वेटयति । Desi. विवेटिषति or विविटिषति । Inten. वेविट्यते । यङ् लुक् वेविटीति, वेवेत्ति । Gerund वेटित्वा or विटित्वा । Nouns : विटः, विटपः ॥

339. ✓ Biṭa (✓ Hiṭa), to swear, to curse, to shout, exclaim, to address harshly.
Pre. बेटति, हेटति । Per. बिबेट, बिहेट, बिबिटतुः, जिहिटतुः, बिबिदुः, शिहिदुः । I Fut. बेटिता । Aor. अबेटीत्, अहेटीत् । Caus. बेटयति, हेटयति । Desi. बिबेटिषति, बिबिटिषति, जिहिटिषति । Inten. बेबिट्यते, जेहिट्यते । यङ् लुक् बेविटीति, बेवेत्ति ॥

340. ✓ Iṭa, 341. ✓ Kiṭa, 342. ✓ Kaṭi, to go. The indicatory long ई in कटी shows that the Sūtra VII. 2. 14 § 3039 applies, and so no इट् augment is added in the Nishṭhā. Some take this root as ending in short इ, therefore they insert a nasal, and conjugate it as कण्टति etc. They analyse कटी as made up of three roots, namely क, इ, and ई. The root इ is thus conjugated: एति, इतः etc. The long ई is similarly conjugated, except that in the Perfect it forms ईयाञ्चकार etc. (III. 1. 36 § 2337).
Pre. — एटति । Per. — ईयाट...

352. ✓ Sphuṭir, to burst or split open; to break forth.
Pre. ‹?› or स्फुटति, स्फोटति । Per. पुस्फोट (?) । I Fut. स्फोटि(ठि)ता । Aorist अपस्फुटत् or अपस्फोटीत् । Desi. ‹?› । Ger. स्फुटित्वा or स्फोटित्वा । As this root has an indicatory इर, the Aorist is formed optionally by adding अङ् (III. 1. 57). Thus अपस्फुटत् or अपस्फोटीत् । Some read the root as स्फुटि and therefore it takes the नुम् augment. As स्फुण्डति । Mādhava gives it as स्फुटिर । Candra reads स्फुट । Its Aorist is not formed in अङ् । Kṣīrasvāmī and Kāśyapa give three roots स्फुट, स्फुडि and स्फुटिर ॥

गण्ड: 'cheek.' According to some the last five roots (including gaṇḍa) are incapable of conjugation. Nouns only are formed from them.

Here end the roots whose final is a letter of the palatal class.

अथ पवगीयान्ताः । तत्रानुदात्तेतः स्तोभत्यन्ताश्चतुस्त्रिंशत् ॥

Now we give the roots ending in a labial. Of these, thirty-four up to Stubha are anudāttet.

तिपृ ३८५ तेपृ ३८६, टिपृ ३८७, ष्टेपृ ३८८ क्षरणार्थाः । ‹?› अनुदात्तः । क्षीरस्वामी स्वयं सेडिति बभ्राम । तेपते । तितिपे । क्रादिनियमादिट् । तितिषिषे । तेप्ता । तेप्स्यते ॥

The first of these roots is anudātta also and hence अनिट् । Kshīrasvāmī mistook it as सेट् ।

Thus Pre. तेपते । Per. तितिपे । Though this is aniṭ, yet in the Second and First Person would be added by the rule of kryādi (VII. 2. 15, S. 2293). Therefore, we have तितिषिषे and तितिषिवहे ॥ The First Future is तेप्ता । The Second Future is तेप्स्यते ।

In forming the Benedictive the following rule applies:—
entries.note: Tail continuation of SK 2299 from preceding page.

entries.english:
2300. After roots ending in a consonant, that adjoins a vowel of ik pratyāhāra, the substitutes of liṅ (III. 3. 161) and sich (III. 1. 44) when they begin with a consonant of jhal pratyāhāra, are kit, when the ātmanepada affixes follow.

Note:—The sūtra consists of two words लिङ्‌सिचौ and आत्मनेपदेषु, literally meaning "the affixes liṅ and sich in the Ātmanepada." The other phrases, given in the above text must be supplied from the previous sūtras, to complete the sense. The anuvṛitti of the word सम्, that began with sūtra, I. 2. 8. does not extend further. भित्सीष्ट 'may he break' and भुत्सीष्ट 'may he know,' अभित्त, अभुत्त 'he broke, he knew.'

Thus the root तिप् ends with a simple consonant, is preceded by a letter of ik pratyāhāra; after this root the jhalādi affix सीयुट् of the Benedictive in the Ātmanepada is treated like कित्; therefore there is no guṇa substitution of the vowel of the root before this affix. तिप् + सीष्ट = तिप्सीष्ट ॥ So also तिप्सीयास्ताम्, तिप्सीरन् ॥

Similarly in the Aorist we have अ + तिप् + स् + त, the स् of the Aorist being elided by VIII. 2. 26, S. 2281: अतिप्त । अतिप्साताम् । अतिप्सत ॥

त्रपूष ३९९ लज्जायाम् । त्रपते ॥

The Present is त्रपते । In forming the Perfect, the following rule applies.

2301. ए is substituted for the अ of तृ, फल, भज and त्रप, and the reduplicate is elided, when the affixes of the Perfect having an indicatory क् (or ङ्) follow, as well as when थल् with the इट् augment follows.

Thus (तेतुः, तेतु, तेतिथ; फेलतुः, फेलुः, फेलिथ; भेजतुः, भेजुः, भेजिथ), त्रेपे, त्रेपाते, त्रेपिरे ॥

2303. The affix आय comes without changing the sense, after गुपू 'to protect,' धूप 'to heat,' विच्छ 'to approach,' पण 'to praise' and पन् 'to praise.'
(

NOTE:— Thus गोपायति 'he protects'; धूपायति 'he heats'; so also, विच्छायति, पणायति, and पनायति.

NOTE.— The verb being read along with 'to praise,' has here the sense of praise only; so that the affix does not come after the verb ‹?› when it means 'to make a contract'; as शतस्य पणते, सहस्रस्य पणते.

NOTE:— The verbs in ‹?› do not take Âtmanepada affixes, as there is no indicatory letter to show that.

Thus गुप् + आय् ।

Now applies S. 2189 and we get the guna of उ; as, गोपाय ।

entries.english:
2304. All the words ending with the affixes ‹?› and the rest are called Dhâtus.

NOTE:— This extends the sphere of Dhâtus or roots already defined in Sûtra I. 3. 1. These roots may be called derivative roots. They are separate independent roots, and have all the functions of a root, as taking tense-affixes &c. as shown in the above examples. Thus चिकीर्षति 'to wish to do,' कारयति 'to cause to do'; चेक्रियते 'to do repeatedly' are separate roots and not the same as कृ, 'to do'; and thus take लट् &c.

The stems that take the affixes beginning with ‹?› and ending with ‹?› namely, the following 1. ‹?› (III. 1. 5, 6, 7) 2. ‹?› (III. 1. 8) 3. ‹?› (III. 1. 9), 4. ‹?› (III. 1. 11) 5. ‹?› (III. 1. 13), 6. ‹?› (III. 1. 20) 7. ‹?› (III. 1. 21), 8. ‹?› (III. 1. 22) 9. ‹?› (III. 1. 25) 10. ‹?› (III. 1. 27), 11. ‹?› (III. 1. 28), 12. ‹?› (III. 1. 29), and 13. ‹?›, (III. 1. 30) are called also roots. Being roots they are conjugated in लट्, लिट् &c.

Thus Pres. ‹?› sutras apply:—

entries.english:
2305. The affixes ‹?› and those that follow it, (i.e. ‹?›) are optionally added, when it is desired to express one'self with an ârdhadhâtuka affix.

NOTE:— Thus तास् 3rd. sing. of the Future is an ârdhadhâtuka affix. It is optional to retain the âya of gopâya before this affix. So we have गोपायिता or गोप्ता 'he will protect'. So also ऋतीता or ऋतीयिता; कमिता or कामयिता.

But for this sutra, the affixes ‹?› &c. would have come always even when Ârdhadhâtuka affixes were to be applied. This makes it optional. Therefore the proper ârdhadhâtuka affixes should be applied when we retain ‹?› &c. and when we do not retain them. Thus the ârdhadhâtuka ‹?› (III. 3. 95) will be employed in forming the feminine noun from the simple root, but the Ârdhadhâtuka ‹?› (III. 3. 102) will be employed in forming the feminine when ‹?› &c. are retained.

Thus गुप्तिः or गोपा,

entries.english:
2306. आम् is the affix of the verb कास् 'to cough,' and of those roots that are formed by affixes (i. e. the derivative verbs), when लिट् follows, except in the Mantra.

NOTE:— This forms the Periphrastic Perfect. The perfect of कास् will be कासाम्, after which the terminations of the Perfect are all elided (II. 4. 81) and instead, the perfect tense of the auxiliary verb कृ or भू or अस् is added. As कासाञ्चक्रे 'he coughed'; चोरयाञ्चकार 'he stole.' So also ‹?›.

This rule however does not apply to the Vedas; as Rig Veda I. 79. 2.

Vârt:— This rule only applies where the root is polysyllabic consisting of more than one vowel; as चुलुम्पाञ्चकार, दरिद्राञ्चकार । The force of this vartika is that even of non-derivative roots, the Perfect will be formed periphrastically if the root consists of more than one syllable. In fact, the vârtika would substitute the word anekâchaḥ in the room of pratyayât. The sutra would then run thus: "kâsânekâcha âm amantre liṭi": "आम् is added to the root kâs and to roots of more than one syllable in the Perfect; but not in the Vedas."

entries.english:
2307. From this upto VI. 4. 68 inclusive, is always to be supplied "before an affix called ârdhadhâtuka (III. 4. 114 &c)."

NOTE:— This is an adhikâra sûtra and extends upto VI. 4. 69 (exclusive). In all the sûtras upto VI. 4. 68 should be supplied the phrase "before an affix called ârdhadhâtuka." Thus VI. 4. 48 teaches "the अ standing at the end of a verbal stem is elided." To complete the sense we should add: "before an ârdhadhâtuka affix." Thus the final अ of the verbal stem चिकीर्ष is elided before the ârdhadhâtuka affix तृच्, as चिकीर्षिता, चिकीर्षितुम्; but the final is not elided before a sârvadhâtuka affix, as the अ of भू in भवति, भवतः. The luk-elision of शप् after roots of अदादि class, implies that there is never lopa of अकार.

Kârikâ:—
लोपो यलोपोऽथ णिलोपश्च प्रयोजनम् ।
आल्लोप ईत्वमेत्वं च चिण्वद्भावश्च सेधुटि ॥

The following purposes are served by this sutra, i. e. an ârdhadhâtuka affix causes the following special changes: (1) अलोपः—The elision of अ of a stem, as shown above, in चिकीर्षिता, चिकीर्षितुम्. (2) यलोपश्च । The elision of य by VI. 4. 49, 50: as बेभिदिता, बेभिदितुम्, बेभिदितव्यम् from the intensive stem. Before Sârvadhâtuka, we have बेभिद्यते, चेच्छिद्यते । (3) णिलोपश्च प्रयोजनम् । The elision of णि by VI. 4. 51, as कारणा, हारणा, पाच्यते (पाचि + यक् + ते = पाच + य + ते), पाक्यते । In Sârvadhâtuka, पाचयति, याजयति, कारयति, हारयति । (4) आल्लोपः—the elision of आकार, VI. 4. 64: पपतुः, पपुः, ववतुः, वपुः । In Sârvadhâtuka, यान्ति, वान्ति । (5) ईत्वम्—The substitution of long ई for आकार in some roots, VI. 4. 65: as दीयेताम्, दीयेरन्; in Sârvadhâtuka प्रदाताम्, प्रधाताम् । (6) एत्वम्—The substitution of ए for आकार, VI. 4. 68; as म्लेयात्, ग्लेयात्; in Sârvadhâtuka, स्नायात्, ग्लायात् । This is confined to the Precative (âśîrliṅ). (7) चिण्वद्भावश्च सेधुटि—The treatment of the Precative like Aorist Passive in चिण् by VI. 4. 62, as कारिषीष्ट, हारिषीष्ट । In Sârvadhâtuka क्रियेत, ह्रियेत ।

entries.english:
2308. The अ standing at the end of a stem is elided before an Ârdhadhâtuka affix.

NOTE:— Thus चिकीर्षिता, चिकीर्षितुम् and चिकीर्षितव्यम्, from the Desiderative stem चिकीर्ष । So also धिनुतः and कृणुतः from the roots धिन्व् and कृण्व्; thus धिन्व् + उ (III. 1. 80) = धिन् + अ + उ (III. 1. 80) = धिन् + उ (अ being elided before the ârdhadhâtuka उ) = धिनु, the 3rd Personal dual of it is धिनुतः । The addition of अ by III. 1. 80 and its subsequent elision by the present sûtra, may appear a redundancy, but the elided अ being sthânivat, prevents guṇa of धि । So also कृणुतः । See sûtra III. 1. 80. Why do we say 'the अ is elided'? Observe चेता, स्तोता here इ and उ have not been elided. Why do we say 'तः with a त'? The long आकार will not be elided: as याता, वाता । Why do we say 'before an Ârdhadhâtuka'? Before Sârvadhâtuka there will be no elision of अ, nor before a Taddhita: as पचथम् and वृक्षता ॥

Vârt:— The elision of such अ takes place even to the supersession of the subsequent rules relating to Vṛiddhi and lengthening. As चिकीर्षकः, जिहीर्षकः, चिकीर्ष्यते and जिहीर्ष्यते ॥

Thus गोपाय + आम् + चकार = गोपायाञ्चकार or गोपायां बभूव or गोपायामास । The affix आय being optional before लिट् (III. 1. 31. S. 2305) we have the alternative forms जुगोप, जुगुपतुः । The root गुपू has an indicatory ऌ and so the इट् augment is optional (VII. 2. 44. S. 2279). As जुगोपिथ or जुगोप्थ । The लुट् is गोपायिता or गोपिता or गोप्ता । The लिङ् is गोपाय्यात् or गुप्यात् । The लुङ् is अगोपायीत् or अगोपीत् or अगौप्सीत् ॥

entries.english: 438. √ trumpha, To injure, to hurt. Pre. त्रुम्फति । Per. तुत्रुम्फ । I Fut. त्रुम्फिता । Aorist अत्रुम्फीत् । Caus. त्रुम्फयति । Desi. तुत्रुम्फिषति । Inten. तोत्रुम्फ्यते । Note:—The nasal in the above roots is not elided in the Perfect because the affixes are here added to a root ending in a conjunct consonant, and they are not kit (I. 2. 5. S. 2242). Therefore we have the forms तुतुम्प &c. For the rule of elision of nasal (VI. 4. 24. S. 415) applies to kit or ṅit affixes. In the Benedictive, the affixes being kit by III. 4. 104 S. 2216, there is elision of the nasal (VI. 4. 24. S. 415). Thus तुप्यात् from तुम्प ॥ When preceded by प्र the root तुम्प adds a sibilant in its beginning, because of the following vārtika to be found in the Pāraskarādi class (VI. 1. 157 S. 1071):— Gaṇa Vārtika:—The augment सुट् is added to the root तुम्प when preceded by the preposition प्र provided the agent of the notion is a cow. Thus प्रस्तुम्पति गौः ॥ (प्रस्तुम्पति इति प्रवृत्ते सुट् Padamañjarī.) Since the root is exhibited in the above Vārtika as प्रस्तुम्पति with शितप्, therefore when this root is conjugated in यङ्-लुक् the sibilant is not added (VII. 2. 10 S. 2646). Thus प्रतोतुम्पीति ॥

entries.english:
2309. म् is substituted for the म् of a root before the affixes beginning with म and व ॥

NOTE:—As the Imperfect of भ्रम्, as in the sentence ‹?›. The व् is elided as a Vedic diversity. So also with क्षम्, the augment इट् is not added by the option allowed, owing to VII. 2. 44. This sūtra applies to those cases where the म् is not at the end of a word, as it was in the last sūtra.

Thus from the root क्षम् we have in the perfect 1st person dual चक्षन्वहे । But when the intermediate इट् is not added, then the म् is changed to न् and then to अनुस्वार. As चक्षमिषे or चक्षंसे; so also in the plural, चक्षमिध्वे or चक्षन्ध्वे ॥

Aorist अचङ्क्षमीत् । Past Part. Pass. क्षान्तः । Ger. क्षमित्वा or क्षान्त्वा । Infini. क्षमितुम् or क्षन्तुम् । Nouns क्षमः । F. क्षमा, क्षमकः ॥

470. कम् कान्तौ । The word Kānti here means 'desire.' The root therefore means 'to desire, long for, wish.' The following sūtra applies to its conjugation.

entries.english:
2310. The affix णिङ् comes without changing the sense after the root कम् 'to desire.'

The ङ् indicates vṛddhi (VII. 2. 115) and ङ् shows that the root takes the affixes of the Ātmanepada; as, कामयते 'he desires'; so also कामयेते and कामयन्ते ॥

The Perfect is formed periphrastically by आम् which being an ārdhadhātuka affix required the elision of णि of the root by VI. 4. 51, § 2313. But the following sūtra prevents the elision:—

2311. अय् is substituted for the णि of णिङ्, before the affixes आम्, अन्त, आलु, आय्य, इत्स्नु, and ष्णुक ॥

Note:—Thus कारयाञ्चकार, हारयाञ्चकार, मण्डयन्तः मण्डयन्तः (formed by the Jhac affix झ = अन्त; added to the roots मण्ड and मन्त्र) धातु । पहयालुः । आय्य—उपायाय्यः सहायाय्यः । इत्स्नुः—स्तनयित्स्नुः । ष्णुक—पोषयिष्णुकः ॥

Note:—This sūtra could have been well dispensed with for the affix णि would take guṇa ए which will be changed to अय् by the rules of Sandhi, before these affixes. The substitution of अय् for णि is for the sake of the subsequent sūtra VI. 4. 56, § 2336 however, because there णि could not be changed to अय् by any sandhi-rules.

The णि is always changed to अय्; therefore the अय् substitution of the present sūtra would have been redundant, but it is taught here in order to supersede the elision declared hereafter in VI. 4. 51, § 2313. Thus कामयां ‹?›

The addition of आय being optional (III. 1. 31, § 2305) we have the alternative form चकमे also.

The Future forms are:—कामयिता or कमिता । कामयिष्यते or कमिष्यते ॥

In forming the Aorist, the following sūtra applies.

entries.english: 2312. After a root which ends in णि (III. 1. 20, 21, 44, &c.) and after the verb श्रि 'to service,' द्रु 'to run,' and स्रु 'to drop,' चङ् is the substitute of च्लि, when लुङ् follows signifying an agent. NOTE:— The ङ् prevents guṇa and vṛiddhi: अ is to distinguish it from ‹?›. When चङ् is added there is reduplication (VI. 1. 11). The usual terminations of the Imperfect are employed after the root, when चङ् is used; as, अचीकरत् 'he caused to make'; अशिश्रियत् 'he served or went'; अदुद्रुवत् 'he ran'; असुस्रुवत् 'it flowed.' This form is not used in Passive; as, ‹?›. Thus ‹?›. Now applies the following sûtra, by which the (णि) is elided.
entries.note: Devanagari sutra line was printed on preceding page; entry continues on this page.

entries.english: 2313. The णि of the verbal stem formed with the affix णि, is elided before an ârdhadhâtuka affix which does not take the augment इट् ॥ NOTE:— This debars the semi-vowel य्, the guṇa, vṛiddhi and the long substitutions. Thus अशशमत्, अशीशमत्, आटिटत्, कारणा, हारणा, कारकः, हारकः, कार्यते, हार्यते and कारयिता (see VII. 4. 1 for the shortening of the stem of the Aorists in these). Why do we say 'not having the augment इट्'? Observe कारयिता and हारयिता ॥ The sûtra VI. 4. 82, S. 272 (a semi-vowel is substituted for the final इ or ई of a root before a vowel-beginning affix &c.) being subsequent in order of Ashṭâdhyâyî would debar the present sûtra and prevent the elision of णि and cause य् to be substituted instead. This however is prevented by the following. Vârtika:— The rule ordaining the elision of णि (S. 2313) and that teaching the elision of अ (VI. 4. 48, S. 2308) take effect even to the supersession of the subsequent rules ordaining इयङ् (VI. 4. 78, S. 2290), or semi-vowel (VI. 4. 82, S. 272), or guṇa, (VII. 3. 84, S. 2168 &c.) or vṛiddhi, (VII. 2. 115, S. 254), or lengthening. NOTE:— The elision of अ supersedes only the two rules of vṛiddhi, lengthening and not the others. The elision of (णि) supersedes all the above five rules of iyaṅ, yaṇ, guṇa, vṛiddhi and lengthening. Q. There is no necessity for this vârtika with regard to णि, for if the five rules mentioned above were not to be superseded by णि-elision, then this rule will find no scope anywhere. And as scope must be given to every rule, the present sûtra inferentially and necessarily supersedes the above rules. Ans. The vârtika is not unnecessary. The णि elision finds its unrestricted scope before the ârdhadhâtuka affixes like क्तिन् (III. 3. 174, S. 3313). Thus from शमि we have शान्तिः, from √ तमि तन्तिः. The intermediate इट् is prevented there by VII. 2. 9, S. 3163. Hence if this vârtika were not taught, the णि would be elided only before the ârdhadhâtuka kṛit affix क्तिन् and no where else. As a matter of fact, the force of the word अनिटि in the sûtra is that the rule of the elision of णि applies to all ârdhadhâtuka affixes, and not only to a single affix क्तिन्. NOTE:— Had the present sûtra not superseded इयङ् &c., then it would have been more proper to draft it as णेः only without the word अनिटि । For the sûtra with the anuvṛitti of आर्धधातुके read into it, would apply to the affix क्तिन्, only after the rules yaṇ &c. had restricted its scope. So there would be no necessity of adding अनिटि. The very fact that the word अनिटि is added shows that the sûtra has for its scope all ârdhadhâtuka affixes, and therefore it is an exception by anticipation to the rules of iyaṅ &c. Thus, इयङ् is superseded in अशिश्रियत्. It is a चङ् Aorist. There is no scope for guṇa here, as चङ् is ङित् and yaṇ of sûtra VI. 4. 82, S. 272 has also no scope, as the इ (णि) in श्रि is preceded by a conjunct consonant. The only rule left that would have applied to this णि is इयङ्. The present vârtika debars इयङ् but causes the elision of इ (णि) ॥ Similarly यण् (semivowel) substitution is superseded in आटिटत् । Guṇa is superseded in अशशमत् and vṛiddhi in कारकः and lengthening in कार्यते ॥ Now applies the following. Thus ‹?›

entries.english: 2314. A short is substituted for the vowel, standing in a penultimate position, in the णि-formed stem; when the affix चङ् (of the Reduplicate Aorist) follows. Thus ‹?› (VI. 4. 51, S. 2313) = ‹?› (VII. 4. 1, S. 2314). Now applies the following sûtra which causes reduplication.

2315. Of a non-reduplicate root there is reduplication when the affix चङ् of the Aorist follows. Dr. Ballantyne translates it this:— "When चङ् follows, there are two in the room of the first portion, containing a single vowel, of an unreduplicated root; but the reduplication is of the second portion of a root that begins with a vowel." The first syllable is reduplicated if the first portion of the root begins with a consonant; the second syllable is reduplicated if the first portion begins with a vowel. Thus ‹?› Now applies the following atideśa sûtra.

2316. In the reduplicated Aorist of the णि-stems, the reduplicate adapts itself to that of the Desiderative, when the vowel of the root is light, and the root has not lost its end-vowel before the णि affix. The word चङ्परे is a Bahuvrîhi compound and therefore it means णि. This word णि so qualified, as well as the word अङ्गस्य should both be twice employed in this sûtra, in order to give the full meaning. We explain therefore the sûtra thus:— "that णि which is followed by that affix which gives the designation of अङ्ग to the root"—this is one portion. The next part is—"a short vowel which follows such णि, and the abhyâsa of the aṅga which follows such short vowel of that abhyâsa, the operations are like those of the Desiderative, before the णि, when no अक्-vowel is elided." Or the word अङ्गस्य is not repeated. Then the sûtra would mean 'that aṅga which stands before that णि which is followed by चङ्; the abhyâsa of such an aṅga, when followed by a short vowel,—on that abhyâsa, the operations are like those of the Desiderative &c.' NOTE:— Dr. Ballantyne has translated this sûtra as follows:— "Let the effect be like as if सन् (III. 1. 7, S. 2608) had followed, on the reduplicate, if followed by a light vowel of an inflective base to which णि followed by चङ् is affixed provided there is not the elision of any letter in the pratyâhâra अक् occasioned by the affixing of णि (as, for example under the provisions of VI. 4. 48, S. 2308)." NOTE:— The words of this sûtra require a little detailed explanation. The word सन्वत् means "like unto सन् or Desiderative"; i. e. as the Desiderative is treated, so should the चङ् Aorist of the णि stems. The words लघुनि and चङ्परे are both in the Locative case, but not in apposition with each other, but refer to different objects. लघुनि means 'when a light vowel follows,' namely that reduplicate which is followed by the light root-vowel. The operations to be performed on such a reduplicate, in the चङ् Aorist, after the णि, are the same, as on the reduplicate of the Desiderative, अनग्लोपे "provided that a simple vowel of the Pratyâhâra अक् has not been elided." We read the word णि into this sûtra, because there can be no other root which will form a चङ् Aorist. णि stems form such Aorist, (III. 1. 48), as well as the simple roots श्रि, द्रु and स्रु. The word चङ्परे is a Bahuvrîhi and qualifies the word णि understood: that stem which is followed by चङ्; therefore, it refers to the णि stem, and not to the simple roots śri, dru and sru. The light vowel, therefore, refers to the light vowel of the णि-stem before चङ्. The word अनग्लोपे is in apposition with चङ्परे । Thus कम् + णिच्, (III. 1. 30) = चकाम् + णिच् + अत् (III. 1. 48) = अकाम् + अत् (VI. 4. 51) = अकमत् (VII. 4. 1) = अचकम् + अत् (VI. 1. 11). Then applies the next sûtra. NOTE:— Thus VII. 4. 79 teaches the substitution of ‹?› for ‹?› in the reduplicate of the Desiderative. The same substitution will take place in the reduplicate of the Aorist: as ‹?› Thus by VII. 4. 80, is substituted for

Observe प्रततक्षत्, अजागरत् ॥
By sûtra III. 1. 48 : 2313 the roots श्वि, ‹?› and सु also form चङ् aorist. The sanvadbhâva however does not take place with regard to these roots: because these roots do not get the designation of अङ्ग before चङ् । The rule is therefore confined to णि-roots, for these are the roots which get the designation अङ्ग before the affix चङ् । Moreover the reduplicate must be that of the ‹?›, which can be of णि-roots only.

NOTE:—As पिपचिषति, विवक्षिषति, (VIII. 2. 36, 41) चिखादिषति, विविदिषति ॥ Why do we say in the Desiderative ? Observe पपाच ॥ Why do we say 'for the ‹?›' ? Observe लुलूषति ॥ Why do we say 'short ‹?›' ? Observe पापचिषते the Desiderative of the Intensive पापच्यते ॥
Therefore अचिकम् + अत, अचिकम् + अत, because चङ् is considered like सन् ॥
